2467.content: Pneumatic mail — Carries things between chests and machines in capsules through tubes.

2468.content: Auto-assembler — Makes one chosen thing again and again by a recipe card.

2469.content: Interworld channel — Links the storages of two worlds: you see the far one’s things and take them.

2470.content: Lift — A cabin that carries you and others between floors.

2471.content: Jump beacon — Jumps you between your bases inside one world.

2472.content: Courier drone — A drone carries things between two storages where no tube reaches.

2473.content: Knapsack — A worn store that also keeps the suit supplied.

2474.content: Launch Gantry — Fills a rocket, shuttle or bell by hose, straight from fuel pipes.

2475.content: Charging Gantry — Charges the batteries of a rocket on its table straight from the grid.

2476.content: Star map and a flight — From the cockpit of a rocket you choose a world on the star map and launch.

2477.content: Building a rocket — A rocket is built block by block on a launch table; each next one flies farther.

2478.content: Rocket modules — Modules go into sockets on the hull and decide whether you can come back.

2479.content: Rift Shuttle — Goes from the End through open rifts into four worlds and comes home by its thread for free.

2480.content: Diving Bell — Dives from the Nether through lava to four worlds at the bottom of the vents; the winch hauls it home for free.

2481.content: Rovers — A ground vehicle for other worlds: seats, cargo, air around it; folds into a pocket capsule.

2482.content: Flying a ship — Take off, leave the sky for open space, land — and what each key of the cockpit does.

2483.content: Jump and system map — Crosses thousands of blocks in four seconds.

2484.content: Shipyard: building a ship — The shipyard builds ships, raises their class and takes them apart.

2485.content: Ship console — One window for the hold, modules, fuel, repair, friends and live cargo of a ship.

2486.content: Friends and crew of a ship — Lets other players aboard, to the helm or to the console — even while you are offline.

2487.content: Ship Beacon — Calls your ship to you from wherever it stands.

2488.content: Ship modules — Modules make a ship faster, tougher and roomier; each kind has three tiers.

2489.content: Raising a ship’s class — C → B → A → S: every class makes the same ship better in everything.

2490.content: The deck of a ship — Every ship has an interior you can walk while it flies.

2491.content: Autopilot — Flies the ship through space by itself while you walk the deck.

2492.content: System map — A view from above on the space you are in: worlds, belts, stations and your finds.

2493.content: Landing Beacon — A ship from space enters the sky right above it — no more landing thousands of blocks from home.

2494.content: Live cargo — Carries animals, villagers and other creatures between worlds aboard your ship.

2495.content: Crossing from ship to ship — A sleeve of light carries you to another ship in space or on the ground.

2496.content: Salvage: a ship in the hold — The grapple folds an empty ship into your hold. No module is needed.

2497.content: Tow — A rope of light drags a ship with people aboard, or one that does not fit your hold.

2498.content: Belt ores and the mining beam — Ores that no world has hang in space: mine them with a pickaxe or from the cockpit.

2499.content: Wrecked ships — Remains of old expeditions: a chest, a story, and sometimes a ship you can raise.

2500.content: Ship weapons — The pulse cannon: a beam that hits where you aim at once.

2501.content: Heavy weapons and shield — A piercing slug, homing torpedoes and a shield that takes hits before the hull.

2502.content: Weapons of the roads — The void lance, the slag flak, and flares against torpedoes.

2503.content: Freighter: docking, key, jumps — A capital ship that carries your ships, your stores and your base, and comes when called.

2504.content: Freighter decks — Inside: a hangar, a build hall, a hold in one storage network, crew rooms and a bridge with a view of space.

2505.content: Buying and exchanging a freighter — Every station of a people sells three freighters a day and takes yours in exchange.

2506.content: Distress call — Save a freighter from the Drifters — the first one saved becomes yours.

2507.content: Fleet and expeditions — Frigates follow your freighter and go on expeditions by themselves, even while you are offline.

2509.content: Stations of the peoples — Where a ship is refueled, mended and raised in class away from home, and where pilots trade.

2510.content: Station orders — Paid work from the order board: supply of the road, emeralds and the trust of the people.

2511.content: Ring race — A race around a station through twelve rings of light.

2512.content: Trust and the vault — How peoples start to trust you, what each step opens and how to get the key of a station vault.

2513.content: Launching your own station — An emitter on the ground sends a seed into orbit, and the core of your station gathers there from light.

2514.content: Growing the station — Each tier adds four sockets and room for more modules.

2515.content: Station modules — What each module of your station does and how its console is used.

2516.content: Station crew — Natives who move into your station and help its work.

2517.content: Trade routes — Cargo drones carry what your station makes to the peoples and bring emeralds and supply.

2518.content: Observatory projects — Anomaly data and samples turn into new recipes: ship modules, the pocket sun, the magnetic shield.

2519.content: Pocket Sun — A tiny sun from the observatory: it feeds a station of level “Ring”.

2520.content: Taking the station apart — Takes off a module, the lowest tier or the whole station and gives everything back.

2521.content: Outside the ship in space — How to leave the ship in zero gravity, move there and come back alive.

2522.content: Zero-G Forge and star gear — Forges the gear of the stars and the armor of the roads from metals floating in a chamber.

2523.content: Fighting Drifters — How Drifters appear, how to aim, and how to take one of their ships whole.

2526.content: The rockgnawer swarm — Hungry rockgnawers catch ships that loiter among asteroids: how to shake them off or shoot them.

2528.content: The comet — How to catch a comet and get ice and a comet core.

2529.content: Life of open space — Creatures of open space, the Interrift and the Depths: where they live, what they do to a ship and what they leave.

2530.content: Sky anomalies — Phenomena of space: how to notice, visit and study them, and which are dangerous.

2537.content: Village crafts — Villagers of five new trades; their work blocks are machines of this mod.

2538.content: Natives: talking and trading — Each of the worlds has its own people: they talk, trade, sell maps and keep tasks for you.

2539.content: Native tasks — Natives give tasks: bring, defeat, find, survive, deliver — and pay with things nobody else sells.

2540.content: Finding structures of the worlds — Structures of a world hide loot of that world and pages for the journal about the place.

2541.content: Dungeons: in, down and out — A dungeon of a world is several floors with a locked gate on each, a guard, and the master with a treasury at the bottom.

2542.content: Dungeons: seals and locks — What the seals in dungeons and ruins wait for and how each lock works.

2543.content: Dungeons: what each one is about — Every big dungeon has one mechanism of its own on all its floors; a change is seen and heard 3–6 seconds ahead.

2544.content: Masters of worlds: how to summon

2546.content: World gates — Awakened gates are linked: from any of them you step to any other, for a small toll.

2547.content: World events — Every few days something big happens in a world; who stays there to the end has survived it.

2548.content: Weather of the worlds — Weather comes and goes by itself and slightly changes the world: what you breathe, see, and how you move.

2549.content: Ores of the worlds — Each world has two or three ores of its own in its own rock; they pay for almost everything the worlds give.

2550.content: Food and plants of the worlds — Plants and beasts of a world give food that helps to live in it: warmth, coolness, acid resistance, air.

2551.content: Breeding beasts of worlds — Some beasts eat from your hand, and a fed pair has young — only under the sky of their own world.

2552.content: Taming and riding — Feed a creature that can be tamed until it trusts you; in a harness of its world it carries you on land, in the air or water.

2553.content: Atlas of Life — The Atlas tab of the journal holds a card for every creature: where it lives, what it eats and how to keep it.

2554.content: Meteorites: find and dig — Once in a few days a meteorite falls in wild country, far from homes; it leaves a crater, metal and stardust.

2555.content: Sky Heart — A giant that is not a stone: under the open sky it gathers stardust by night.

2556.content: The way to Thalassia — Thalassia is a second Earth by the star Hemera; the way there is a mouth by Jupiter’s Trojans; the first starship will do.

2557.content: Thalassians and their fields — Thalassians live in hamlets on the meadows above the shallows and trade what keeps a second Earth useful.

2558.content: Garden under the tide — Six plants of Thalassia’s sea live in tidewater; sea grapes are planted in any pond of it.

2559.content: Hemera oil and the liquids of Thalassia — Hemera oil seeps out of ochre basalt and is the best natural fuel: a bucket burns longer than lava.

2562.content: Leap from Verona — The cliff of Verona on Miranda is 270 blocks high; a snowdrift below takes a jump without harm.

2563.content: Reading the Ringwrights — Signs on stones by the gates are words: you match pictures to them until the phrase makes sense.

2568.content: The Wow! Signal and the bearing

2569.content: Lightbearer — A blade of light against Shades of Hunger; weak against everything else.

2570.content: Multitool — One charged tool instead of picks and shovels: it mines, cuts, scans and shoots plasma.

2571.content: Module Bench and armor modules — The Module Bench sets modules into sockets of the worlds’ armor and the multitool; they stay when you take the item back.

2572.content: Weapons of the worlds — Weapons of the worlds have an ability and grow with you: every kill raises their mastery.

2573.content: Armor of the worlds — Armor of the worlds is worn in the usual slots over the spacesuit, has sockets and a set bonus.

2574.content: Artifacts — An artifact is a ring, pendant or belt that works while it is worn in a slot of Trinkets or Curios.

2575.content: Radiation on Io — Under the open sky of Io a dose of radiation builds up; the Radiation Screen of the suit stops it entirely.

2576.content: Wings of Titan — In the thick air of Titan a person flies on muscles alone; elsewhere the wings stay folded.

2577.content: Flying to the Interrift — The void above the End where the rifts hang: the way in, what drifts there and home.

2578.content: Diving into the Depths — The rock under the Nether where the vents glow: the way in, what is there and home.

2579.content: What the magma hides — Four echoes in the magmoscope and how they lead to the Crucible.

2581.content: Geodes of the Depths — How to calm a singing crystal and get a whole fire rose, and where the cold geode is.

2584.content: Keel and jacket — The modules of the dark and fiery far roads: what each tier opens.

2587.content: The Sheer, the Sampler, the First Thread

2590.content: Buried World, Iron Ocean, Core Quarry

2591.content: Digging up giants — Vent mouths and the bones of giants in the Nether rock under pressure.

2593.content: Seams of the End — Sewn seams, splits with rift goods and the endermen’s gathering.

2594.content: Diving the Void Shoals — How to dive under the islands of the End, catch finds and build over the void.

2597.content: Three radio telescopes on three roads make one night’s image of the Galactic Center.

2603.content: Read the Tablet of Hunger for the blueprint, make a hydrogen maser and place it within six blocks of the receiver of a built radio telescope.

2604.content: Build the same on each road: in the Solar System (Earth, Moon or open space), in the Interrift and in the Depths.

2605.content: Press Right-click on the maser: the console names the hour of the night of Sagittarius. Come back when it starts.

2606.content: In the night hold the main mouse button on the wandering center until a minute of good aim gathers; letting go pauses the count.

2607.content: Make records on the two other roads during the same night and press Right-click on the observatory of your own station with all three in your inventory.

2608.content: A night comes once in four days and lasts a day and a half (30 minutes); the same time on all worlds. The center swings more in the Interrift and the Depths.

2609.content: The maser stands within six blocks to the sides, the receiver from two below to six above the maser. Stand within nine blocks of it.

2610.content: Only three records of one and the same night with all three roads fit; a record is an item, so friends can each bring one.

2611.content: “The maser needs an assembled radio telescope near it” — the telescope is not built or stands too far.

2612.content: “Sagittarius is below the horizon: the dish cannot reach it” — on Earth and the Moon wait until it rises; in space it is always up.

2613.content: The observatory refuses — a record is missing: it needs three roads of one night.

2618.content: Listens to the magma under the Nether and finds vents — roads to four worlds.

2625.content: In the Nether lay nine scorched plates 3×3, put the magmascope on the middle one and two heatproof piers one on the other at each corner.

2626.content: When it is assembled, press Right-click with lava buckets on any part: three buckets.

2627.content: Press Right-click with an empty hand and look around below: press Left-click — a ring runs from the crosshair, and a hollow answers with an echo.

2628.content: Bring the crosshair to the echo and strike again: the nearer the strike, the sharper the echo. Strike right over the vent and its crust shows.

2629.content: Keep the crosshair on the crust: rings close toward its rim. Press Left-click as a ring reaches the rim; each vent has its own rhythm.

2630.content: Left-click — strike the magma, the crust or a fire bubble

2631.content: H — toll for 3 embers: shows the nearest vent

2633.content: The ring reaches 42 degrees from the crosshair, the echo is exact within five. A hit counts within 0.17 second of the beat; six to eight hits break a crust.

2634.content: A bubble rises about every sixteen seconds and gives 1 ember, an open vent 4. Pressing on a bubble catches it and does not strike the crust.

2635.content: Works only in the Nether; day, weather and the rock above do not matter. Lava is not returned if you break the structure.

2636.content: No echo at all — there is no vent within 42 degrees: turn and strike elsewhere, four silent strikes bring the toll prompt.

2637.content: “Off the beat: a crack has healed” — you struck off the beat: one crack closed. Watch the ring and listen to the drum.

2638.content: “The magmascope hears only the magma beneath the Nether” — set it up in the Nether: on Earth it will not start.

2643.content: Two telescopes too heavy for a tripod: they stand on a base of blocks.

2649.content: Lay nine observatory plates 3×3 — flush with the ground is fine — and put a telescope pier on the middle one.

2650.content: Place the astrograph on top of the pier: the structure assembles itself.

2651.content: It is not assembled? Press Right-click: white marks show free places of the scheme, red ones — places taken by other blocks.

2652.content: For a graviscope break the astrograph — the base stays — put a gravity pylon on each corner plate and place the graviscope on the pier.

2653.content: Look through it at night with Right-click, as through any telescope. A black hole bends the light of stars: hold Left-click where it goes around nothing.

2654.content: Zoom: astrograph 4.5 times, graviscope 6. The astrograph finds Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, the graviscope — black holes.

2655.content: A hint line costs 4 stardust in the astrograph and 5 in the graviscope; every stronger telescope sees what the weaker ones do.

2656.content: “It stands in the wrong place” — the base goes one block under the pier: the telescope itself is the top block of three.

2657.content: It sees no sky — something stands above the telescope; glass does not count.

2658.content: A part was broken — put it back, and the telescope assembles again.

2659.content: Guide: The telescope and the sky

2664.content: Shows veins of ores whose standard you have recorded in the laboratory.

2670.content: Record a standard of an ore in the spectral laboratory: iron, copper, gold, redstone, diamond and others.

2671.content: Hold the scanner and press Right-click with Shift: the next standard you know. With a sample in the other hand it takes its standard at once.

2672.content: Press Right-click: the nearest veins flare through the rock, the line names their number and distance.

2673.content: Radius 16 blocks, up to 12 marks, a pulse every 2.5 seconds. The scanner starts with 64 pulses; a pinch of redstone from your inventory gives 16 more.

2674.content: Only what is already loaded around you is searched; nearby blocks of one ore count as one vein.

2675.content: “The scanner needs a standard: study an ore in the laboratory” — no known substance is an ore: study one first.

2676.content: “No charge: the scanner needs redstone dust in your inventory” — put redstone dust into your inventory.

2677.content: Found nothing — there is no ore with that substance within 16 blocks: dig on and scan from another place.

2681.content: Two signals that come by the clock: the way to a magnetar and to Thalassia.

2686.content: Ask “When a signal comes” or look at the almanac of the radio view: it counts to the series and to Pontus.

2687.content: For the series point the dish at Vulpecula before it starts and keep it there; straighten every arc with “Dispersion”.

2688.content: For Pontus point the dish at the ecliptic in Leo and fold the beat with “Folding” while the window lasts.

2689.content: Record Pontus a second time in another window or from another place (Earth, Moon, space): the shift gives the distance and the mouth appears on ship instruments.

2690.content: Series: every fifth day, three to six bursts. Three recorded with the dish on Vulpecula make the navigation record of the magnetar.

2691.content: Pontus: every second sidereal day, for four minutes around its passage of the meridian. Outside the window the beam is silent.

2692.content: A burst is not counted for the magnetar — the dish was not on Vulpecula or the source was below 12 degrees: use the Moon or space.

2693.content: “The same window and the same site: record it on another day or from another site.” — the same window and place: wait for the next one.

2698.content: Every kind of signal is tuned with its own instrument, and the line under the map hints which.

2704.content: Point the dish: under the window name is what is in the beam, under the map — what is heard there; it hints at the instrument.

2705.content: “Narrow” (“Wow!”): keep the mouse on the line for 72 seconds; the other button cuts out a carrier that crawls to it.

2706.content: “Dispersion” (burst): turn the wheel until the arc stands up as a line, then press “RECORD”.

2707.content: “Folding” (pulsar): turn the wheel until slanted strokes stand as a column, then record.

2708.content: “Template” (quasar): drag the comb left until its teeth stand on the weak lines, then record.

2709.content: Wheel or arrows — fine, Shift — coarse

2712.content: Schedule, the same on all worlds: “Wow!” once a sidereal day when Sagittarius crosses the meridian, for 72 seconds; a burst once a day; a series every fifth day.

2713.content: “Wow!” counts clean cells: 12 seconds each, six cells, four needed. Machines nearby bring up to eight carriers, two can be cut at once.

2714.content: A fold needs 3 seconds of collecting, a template 5, longer in interference. A missed burst stays in the buffer for two minutes: “Replay the buffer”.

2715.content: Three pulsars make a navigator: jumps cost 25% less (6% for one). One of them never rises over Earth: listen from the Moon or space.

2716.content: The quasar is written once a day, three days make a reference. “Where to look”, “When a signal comes” and “Which way to tune” cost 3 stardust each.

2717.content: The beam is too low — wait for the source to rise or carry the telescope to the Moon or space.

2718.content: “The signal is not gathered yet” — keep the dish still; a moved dish starts collecting anew.

2719.content: The other button does not cut a carrier — only two filters; wait until a carrier leaves the band.

2723.content: Spectrograph: light of the Sun and worlds

2725.content: Hears what no eye sees, by day and in rain, on Earth, on the Moon and in open space.

2731.content: Get the blueprint: notice three anomalies from space or at the observatory console of your own station, and the codex gives it.

2732.content: Make a receiver, three lattice masts and 48 dish panels.

2733.content: Put three masts one on another and the receiver on top; lay the panels 7×7 around it at its own level. Ghosts show missing blocks.

2734.content: When the last block is placed it assembles itself. Press Right-click on it: the radio view opens.

2735.content: Click the map: the dish turns there. Wait until the line under the window name reads “On target”: the signal is collecting.

2736.content: Works on Earth, on the Moon and in open space of every road. Open sky above the receiver is needed on Earth and the Moon; one observer at a time.

2737.content: The dish does not go below 12 degrees; from space the whole sky is open. Earth looks at 40 degrees north, the Moon at 30 south.

2738.content: Running machines within 24 blocks (nearer — stronger) and a storm are interference: a signal collects up to three times longer.

2739.content: “The dish needs open sky above the receiver.” — no block may stand right above the receiver.

2740.content: Not assembled — press Right-click on the receiver: it says how many panels and masts are missing.

2741.content: You broke a block — panels are hidden parts: break the receiver or a mast, the blocks return.

2746.content: The second telescope: zooms 3 times and shows the planets up to Jupiter.

2751.content: Make the main mirror from two lens blanks and coat it with mirror coating.

2752.content: Put together the old refractor, an eyepiece, a truss tube, the mirror and an equatorial mount.

2753.content: Place it under open sky — it stands by itself — and at night press Right-click.

2754.content: Find Taurus, Gemini and Leo; beside each one waits a planet that does not twinkle: bring the crosshair to it and hold Left-click.

2755.content: Sees all that the refractor saw. A hint line costs 3 stardust, a found constellation pays 4, a planet 3.

2756.content: Needs night, clear weather and open sky, like every star telescope; on the observatory of your own station it needs none of these.

2757.content: Guide: The telescope and the sky

2762.content: Looks into the void of the End and finds rifts — the ways to four worlds.

2769.content: In the End lay a floor of 5×5  with a  in the middle of each side, put two  on its center and the riftscope on top. The scheme is on its journal page.

2770.content: Press Right-click with an eye of ender on each of the four sockets.

2771.content: Press Right-click on the riftscope and look around: sparks of the void flow across the sky toward a rift. Follow them.

2772.content: Near the rift the view ripples and knocks; closer, a seam shows. Hold Left-click at its end and lead the crosshair along it, piece by piece, to the other end.

2773.content: Left-click on a crack in the sky — a void shard

2774.content: H — call: for 3 shards shows the nearest rift

2776.content: Only in the End, under open sky and with all four eyes. Day and weather do not matter.

2777.content: A crack opens about every sixteen seconds; an opened rift pays 4 shards. If the crosshair slips, only the last piece closes.

2778.content: Breaking the base gives the eyes back.

2779.content: “Not built” — the message counts missing blocks; “Show in world” on the scheme marks them.

2780.content: It does not assemble — the base goes first, the riftscope is placed last on top.

2784.content: Burns a sample and shows the lines of its substances; what you know opens recipes and instruments.

2791.content: Bring energy and press Right-click on the laboratory with a sample: ice, bone, iron ingot, ore, gas in a bottle. The tooltip of a sample says so.

2792.content: Wait three seconds (Mk1) for the rainbow on its screen and press Right-click again.

2793.content: Nothing known yet? Click every line of the strip and press “Record a new standard” — the first standard is recorded.

2794.content: Later choose a known standard below: its teeth appear on the ruler. Drag the ruler until every tooth stands on a line.

2795.content: Add standards until every strong line is explained, click the lines left over — they are of a new substance — and press “Identify”.

2796.content: Wheel — move the ruler by 0.1 nm, with Shift by 1 nm

2797.content: Tab — handbook, Enter — identify, Esc — close

2798.content: Far light: the other mouse button on the ruler or the wheel stretches it

2799.content: The scale of every sample is shifted by itself — look at the pattern of lines, not at their place. Each test is a spark: 120 ⚡, and the sample burns when identified.

2800.content: Two unknown substances at once cannot be read: learn one of them from a simpler sample first. Standards: one new each time.

2801.content: Mk1 sees up to 770 nm and parts lines 2.0 nm apart, Mk2 to 900 nm and 1.2, Mk3 0.6, Mk4 0.25. The window says at once if the sample needs a stronger one.

2802.content: A new standard pays 2 stardust, a new sample 1, the whole handbook 16.

2803.content: “It does not add up” — every strong line must be explained or marked, and nothing extra; a tooth off its line counts too.

2804.content: The ruler does not fit — a similar pattern is at another place: drag it to the other end of the strip and let go near a line, it snaps.

2805.content: “Not a sample: a spectrum comes from ore, metal, mineral, bottled gas” — the item is no sample; “Take the sample out” in the window takes a wrong one out.

2807.content: Spectrograph: light of the Sun and worlds

2810.content: Spectrograph: light of the Sun and worlds

2811.content: Catches the light of the sky for the same puzzle as in the laboratory: what is the air there made of.

2817.content: Build a telescope (any star telescope) under open sky.

2818.content: By day press Right-click on it with the spectrograph in hand: the light of the Sun opens as a spectrum.

2819.content: At night look through the telescope with the spectrograph in your inventory, aim at a found planet and press Right-click.

2820.content: Solve the spectrum as in the laboratory: choose standards, fit the ruler, press “Identify”. No spark and no sample.

2821.content: Helium: the Sun’s light, with hydrogen, sodium, calcium and iron already known — they are in water, kelp, bone and iron.

2822.content: Signs of life are in the light of Earth, so it is caught from another world: set a telescope on the Moon and aim at Earth; it needs no finding.

2823.content: The Sun needs open sky, no rain and a place with daylight. During a full solar eclipse the corona is caught the same way.

2824.content: “The telescope cannot see the Sun from here” — a roof or cloud covers the Sun: move the telescope or wait for clear weather.

2825.content: Nothing opens at night — the planet must be found already and stand in the crosshair, and the spectrograph be in your inventory.

2826.content: A catch from orbit: an anomaly in the codex shows its light from a ship with the spectrograph in hand, aim for a second.

2832.content: Finds that open in the laboratory, and parts of creatures that tell how to hit them harder.

2837.content: Look for an unknown mineral, strange alloy or alien dust in chests of ruins and dungeons; masters of worlds and guards carry one for sure.

2838.content: Press Right-click on the spectral laboratory with it and identify it as any spectrum.

2839.content: What was inside goes into your inventory. A known one is opened faster: press “Open the sample”.

2840.content: For a weak spot bring a part of a creature — gland, core, plate, marrow, wax, spores — and identify it: the creature is named.

2841.content: Substances: mineral — lithium and silicon, alloy — iron and titanium, dust — xenon, carbon and silicon. Only one of them may be new to you.

2842.content: Identified part: +15% damage to its creatures, +8% to masters and others with 150 health or more. It is for you only.

2843.content: An opened mineral gives a gem, the alloy ferrotitanium ingots, the dust stardust. Batch opening with Shift takes up to 64.

2844.content: No bonus — hit with the weapon in hand: a trap or a pet’s blow does not count.

2848.content: Keeps the air of Venus and the Breath from eating you around a base. It gives no oxygen.

2854.content: Until you have it, wear a suit with an acid-proof coating: install it at a suit rack.

2855.content: Place the scrubber in the middle of the place you work at and bring energy; no pipes are needed.

2856.content: Press Right-click, set the radius with − and + and press “Show the field”.

2857.content: Radius from 2 up to 6 for Mk1, 9, 12 and 15 for Mk2–Mk4; 1.2 ⚡ a tick for each block of radius.

2858.content: Acid hurts five seconds after you step out without protection. A dome, a sealed room, a cabin and the depth of a dungeon shelter from it too.

2859.content: Still burns in a pool — liquid acid is not air: only the coating of the suit saves from it.

2860.content: Choking inside the field — it only cleans: oxygen comes from a suit, a dome or a room.

2862.content: Suit modules: which for which world

2866.content: Turns plants into oxygen: the first source of air for a base and a suit.

2872.content: Place the bioreactor and bring energy: a generator or battery right beside it, or a beam.

2873.content: Press Right-click and put feed into the panel: kelp, leaves, crops, moss, flowers, fruits and plants of other worlds.

2874.content: Lay oxygen pipes from any side of it to an oxygen tank, an air blower, a dome or a suit rack.

2875.content: For automation put a hopper with feed above it.

2876.content: Mk1 makes 4 oxygen a tick for 8 ⚡; every next version is twice as fast. One player breathes 1 a tick.

2877.content: Oxygen from one item: kelp 1,200, dried kelp block 7,200, wheat 160, crops and saplings 90, leaves and flowers 60, seeds and grass 30.

2878.content: Fruits of other worlds give 160–480, wild plants 250–1,400. Air bladders of Venus are twice as quick: 8 a tick for 16 ⚡.

2879.content: Hot feed takes 1.5 times the energy, icy feed is a quarter slower, toxic feed loses a fifth of its oxygen: the panel names the temper.

2880.content: The Catalyst card takes a quarter more from the same feed. A recipe viewer (JEI, REI) lists every feed.

2881.content: It refuses the item — fungi, minerals, animal flesh and dead plants give no oxygen: the panel says which it is.

2882.content: “The oxygen tank is full” — there is nowhere to send oxygen: join a tank or a blower by pipe. Feed is not lost meanwhile.

2883.content: “Not enough energy” — add a generator or take feed that is not hot.

2891.content: Splits water into oxygen and rocket fuel hydrogen, and draws oxygen out of the ground where there is no ice.

2897.content: Place it, bring plenty of energy and an oxygen pipe to a tank or a blower.

2898.content: Give it water in any way: press Right-click with a water bucket, put ice or a bucket into the panel, or bring a pipe.

2899.content: Or place it right against a water source: once a second it scoops the source by itself. A 2×2 well or the sea refills, a lone puddle ends.

2900.content: Put empty canisters into the panel: hydrogen fills them with rocket fuel.

2901.content: No water at all? Put in regolith, rusty sand of Mars, hematite gravel, raw ilmenite or dry ice: the melt gives oxygen and some metal.

2902.content: A bucket of water gives 2,000 oxygen; five buckets fill one canister. Mk1 makes 4 oxygen a tick for 24 ⚡ — three times the price of a bioreactor.

2903.content: Water in items: ice 200, snow block 100, packed ice and a bucket 1,000, blue ice 4,000, water ice of other worlds 500. Ice of methane, nitrogen or ammonia will not do.

2904.content: Rock: 2 oxygen a tick for 32 ⚡. Regolith and rusty sand hold 240, hematite gravel 400, ilmenite 800 and a titanium ingot for sure. Dry ice: 500, 3 a tick for 36 ⚡.

2905.content: An iron nugget is left with a chance: regolith 20%, rusty sand 30%, hematite gravel 60%. Without empty canisters hydrogen past the tank goes out into the air.

2906.content: “The tray is full: empty it” — take out empty buckets and metal, or put a hopper below.

2907.content: “The oxygen tank is full” — it stands with water in it until oxygen has somewhere to go: join a tank by pipe.

2908.content: It does not scoop the spring — there must be room for a whole bucket, and the source must touch one of its sides.

2914.content: Grows crops without soil, water, air or light — and closes the circle of air on a base.

2920.content: Place the bed anywhere: no water or lamp is needed beside it.

2921.content: Press Right-click on its top with seeds: wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, melons, pumpkins, seeds of other mods — or a fruit of another world.

2922.content: Kelp is planted the same way, by Right-click with kelp: it stands in a glass tube and needs no water.

2923.content: Break the ripe plant and plant it again. The bed has no slots: a hopper does not gather from it, harvesters of other mods do.

2924.content: For a base without water: put the harvest into a bioreactor, lead its oxygen to a blower of a sealed room, keep a tank on the pipe.

2925.content: Press Right-click on the bed with phosphate salt: the crop on it is hurried once more.

2926.content: Average time: fruits of other worlds 5 minutes, beetroot 8, wheat, carrots and potatoes 12, kelp 14. It is twice as fast as the best wet farmland.

2927.content: Air for one player or one small room: about 7 beds of Venusian air bladders, 13 of Martian hematite berries, 14 of kelp.

2928.content: In worlds without air ordinary farmland grows nothing, even under a dome. Where you can breathe (Earth, Thalassia, some worlds of the End and Nether roads) it works as usual.

2929.content: A pinch of salt lasts for about two harvests of wheat; green sparks show that the bed is fed.

2930.content: Kelp goes nowhere — press on the top of the bed, and the block above must be air.

2931.content: A sapling or cane does not grow — the bed is for crops: plant those in soil under a dome or in a sealed room.

2937.content: Holds a ball of air without walls: breathe, plant saplings, keep a respawn bed.

2943.content: Place the dome where the middle of the ball should be; walls and ground do not stop the field.

2944.content: Bring an oxygen pipe and energy. Keep a tank on the pipe: when either runs out, the ball is gone.

2945.content: Press Right-click on it and set the radius with the − and + buttons.

2946.content: Press “Show the field” to see how far the air reaches.

2947.content: Radius from 2 up to 6 blocks for Mk1, 9 for Mk2, 12 for Mk3, 15 for Mk4; the Field Amplifier card adds a quarter.

2948.content: Oxygen a tick: 2 for radius 6, 8 for 9, 18 for 12, 35 for 15; energy: 1.5 ⚡ for each block of radius.

2949.content: The Membrane card saves a fifth of the oxygen; a garden of Earth plants in the light gives back up to 35%.

2950.content: Inside there is no heat, cold, acid or radiation of Io, the suit refills by itself, and saplings, sugar cane and kelp grow. Crops still need a hydroponic bed.

2951.content: No ball — the panel shows which is empty: oxygen or energy. Make the radius smaller if the pipe cannot keep up.

2952.content: The bed says there is nothing to breathe — its head lies outside the ball: move it nearer the middle.

2958.content: A room full of air on any world: breathe without a suit, with no heat, cold or acid.

2965.content: Build a closed box of full blocks — floor, walls, roof. Glass, glass panes, oxygen and fuel pipes and the body of any machine in the wall hold air too.

2966.content: Leave an opening two wide and three high, press Right-click on its floor with an airlock door in hand.

2967.content: Stand an air blower inside, away from the outer walls. Bring an oxygen pipe through the wall and energy: a battery beside it or a beam through glass.

2968.content: Press Right-click on the blower: the panel shows the volume of the room. “Sealed, air is in” means you can breathe.

2969.content: For a real airlock put a second door two or three blocks behind the first and open them one at a time.

2970.content: Right-click on the door — open; it closes by itself in three seconds

2971.content: A blower fills 300 blocks of volume (Mk2 600, Mk3 1,200, Mk4 2,400); blowers of one room add up. No room over 20,000 blocks.

2972.content: Every blower takes at least 1 oxygen a tick (2 from 800 blocks on) and 4 ⚡, twice as much energy with each version. The Membrane card saves a fifth of the oxygen.

2973.content: A garden helps: plants of Earth in the light (leaves, crops, flowers, moss) give back up to half the oxygen — for the full half they take 8% of the volume.

2974.content: Where you can breathe (Earth, Thalassia) press “Fills the room”, it turns into “Takes air in”: 3 oxygen a tick for 18 ⚡ go into the pipes. A broken oxygen tank keeps what it holds.

2975.content: Fire needs air: outside a room or dome torches, lanterns, candles and campfires go out, flint and steel only hisses. Light with glowstone, sea lanterns, station lamps.

2976.content: “Air leaks out” — look for slabs, stairs, leaves, ordinary doors, trapdoors, chests in the wall, an open airlock.

2977.content: The leak is not found — wall the room in half with full blocks: the half that reports air is whole, the hole is in the other.

2978.content: It leaks though the walls are whole — the blower itself stands in the wall and blows outside: move it in.

2979.content: “Too big: add a blower” — add a blower or raise its version; the second one needs oxygen and energy too.

2980.content: The door will not stand — all six cells of the opening must be free.

2987.content: Without air and a whole suit you live seconds in another world.

2993.content: Make all four parts and a . Press Right-click on the table and put the parts into its slots: the suit goes under your armor and takes none of its slots.

2994.content: Make air: a bioreactor fed with kelp, leaves or crops, with energy, joined by  to an .

2995.content: Press Right-click on the tank without taking the suit off and keep the window open: a new suit is empty, the tank fills it.

2996.content: For heat and cold put modules into the torso at a suit rack: cooling unit, heating unit, power cell.

2997.content: Works only when all four parts are on. The bare torso holds five minutes of air; a bottle adds ten, a large one twenty.

2998.content: On an airless world the torso also refills by itself: under a dome, in a sealed room, beside a rocket with a life support module. On Earth — only at a tank or a suit rack.

2999.content: The bare suit holds heat and cold for a couple of minutes; acid needs a coating module.

3000.content: You choke in the suit — the tank is empty or one part is missing: the line above the hotbar says which.

3001.content: The suit will not go on from the hand — only at the dressing table.

3004.content: Suit modules: which for which world

3007.content: Suit modules: which for which world

3008.content: Four sockets of the torso decide how long and where you live.

3014.content: Make the modules your next world asks for; the task of its landing stage names them too.

3015.content: Set them at a suit rack, fill oxygen and charge before the flight.

3016.content: Watch the bars above the hotbar: oxygen, charge, and the temperature of the body.

3017.content: Out of air far from home? Light an oxygen candle with Right-click: 1,500 oxygen at once.

3018.content: Moon and Mercury: cooling unit by day, heating unit by night. Venus: cooling unit and coating. Mars, gas giants, ice worlds, open space: heating unit.

3019.content: Io: radiation screen and heating unit, by the lava lakes heat instead. Breath: coating. Forge and Depths: cooling unit. Ash and Interrift: heating unit.

3020.content: Jupiter: antigravity unit. It also spends charge where gravity is only a little over Earth’s: Saturn, Neptune, the Eye, the Lament.

3021.content: Air: the torso holds 5 minutes, a bottle adds 10, a large one 20; a recycler saves a third. Two of the same bottles or cells add up.

3022.content: Charge: a cooling, heating or antigravity unit takes 1 a tick. The torso holds 2,000 (under two minutes), a cell adds 8,000 (almost seven). Solar film gives 3 a tick by day under open sky.

3023.content: Coating and radiation screen need no charge. The thermal unit cools and heats from one socket; its recipe opens after the spectrum of peleite of Io.

3024.content: Hot or cold with the module in — the charge is empty: fill it at a rack or add a cell.

3025.content: Where the bare suit is enough — in the Mycelium’s mild warmth, and for a couple of minutes anywhere: the suit itself takes 60% of heat and cold.

3026.content: The candle refuses — put the suit on or wait: the tank is full.

3033.content: Sets modules into the torso of the suit and fills it with oxygen and charge.

3039.content: Place the rack, bring energy and an oxygen pipe from a tank or a bioreactor.

3040.content: Put the suit on at a dressing table and press Right-click on the rack: the four sockets show the modules of the torso you wear.

3041.content: Put modules into the sockets or take them out: they lie in the torso itself.

3042.content: Keep the window open until “The suit is full”.

3043.content: A spare torso can be put onto the rack itself: it fills without you.

3044.content: Mk1 gives 40 oxygen and 20 charge a tick: an empty bare torso takes about eight seconds. Every version doubles both.

3045.content: A unit of charge costs a unit of energy. The rack itself holds 20,000 oxygen and 20,000 ⚡, more with each version.

3046.content: Take out a bottle or a cell and what no longer fits is lost. A comparator beside the rack reads the oxygen of the torso lying on it.

3047.content: “Put a torso in, or wear the suit” — the suit is not on, or the torso is in your inventory.

3048.content: It shows the modules of another torso — one lies on the rack: take it off, then yours is shown.

3049.content: Charge grows, oxygen does not — no oxygen comes by the pipe: check the tank and the side of the rack.

3051.content: Suit modules: which for which world

3055.content: Makes one chosen thing again and again by a recipe card.

3061.content: Take a blank recipe card in one hand and one of the things you want in the other, and press Right-click: the card remembers its crafting recipe.

3062.content: Several recipes? Press Right-click again: the card goes to the next one.

3063.content: Place the assembler, give it energy, press Right-click on it and put the card into its slot.

3064.content: Put the parts into the tray by hand, hopper from above or the side, or order them by mail: a station beside the assembler, linked to a storage on “On request”.

3065.content: Take the result from the output slot or put a hopper below.

3066.content: One assembly a second for Mk1, 2, 4 and 8 for the others; any assembly costs 400 ⚡. The tray has nine slots and takes no more than a stack of each part.

3067.content: It works with crafting-table recipes of a fixed layout; fireworks and dyeing do not fit. A recipe under a key needs its knowledge to be written.

3068.content: To erase a card press Shift + Right-click with it in hand.

3069.content: “Parts are missing” — the panel shows which part is lacking; the mail asks for it if the storage has it.

3070.content: “Take the finished parts” — take the result: the slot must hold the same thing.

3071.content: “Put in a written recipe card” — the card is blank or the slot is empty.

3077.content: A worn store that also keeps the suit supplied.

3084.content: Keep the knapsack in your inventory, or wear it in the back slot with Trinkets (Curios on NeoForge).

3085.content: Press F9 to open it anywhere, or hold it in your hand and press Right-click.

3086.content: Put things in. “Sort” merges stacks and sorts them.

3087.content: Put cards into the sockets on the right: Pickup, Feed, or a suit’s oxygen bottle or power cell.

3089.content: Slots: 18, 27, 36, 54 by version; card sockets: 1, 2, 3, 4. Upgrading keeps the contents.

3090.content: Pickup sends picked-up things to the same ones in the knapsack. Feed refills the hand when you build and run out.

3091.content: A bottle or cell in a socket tops the suit up once a second when its air or charge is below a quarter, and refills itself from a full suit.

3092.content: Another knapsack and things that do not go into a shulker box do not go in. The knapsack that is open cannot be moved.

3093.content: “No knapsack on you” — it is neither in the back slot nor in the inventory.

3094.content: Cards do not work — the socket opens with the version; the one on the back goes first if you have two.

3099.content: Links the storages of two worlds: you see the far one’s things and take them.

3105.content: Place one quantum cargo node against a storage terminal or cell on the first world and another on the second world. Give both energy.

3106.content: Press Right-click with the tuning fork on one node, travel and press Right-click on the other: a double helix rises — the pair is made. Keep that fork.

3107.content: Open the storage terminal on either world: things of the far end are marked; the tooltip says how many are here and how many there, and how old the list is.

3108.content: To send: put things into the node’s “To send: all goes to the far end” slots (or hopper, pipe): they leave for the far end and unload when that place is loaded.

3109.content: To take: click the thing. The far end wakes for a minute; click again in a couple of seconds and it comes.

3110.content: Things a tick: 2, 8, 32, 128 by version; at most 4,096, 16,384, 65,536 or 262,144 may be on the way. One thing costs 1 ⚡ of the pair’s store of 256,000 ⚡, filled by the energy of both nodes.

3111.content: Waking costs 8 ⚡ a second for each chunk of the zone (0–1–1–2 chunks around by version); it lasts 60 seconds after the last request, at most four far ends at once.

3112.content: Only the owner and their team use a node. Works with Create’s logistics (a Stock Link right against the node) and with AE2 (a cable against it), if those mods stand.

3113.content: Nothing changes for minutes — the far end sleeps; wake it with “Wake the far end” or a click on its thing.

3114.content: “Too little pair charge” — wake needs five seconds’ cost in the store at once: wait for the nodes to charge it.

3115.content: “Cannot wake on this server” — the owner turned the `cargo_wake` rule off: only sending works.

3116.content: Things fell into the tray — no storage touched the far node: put one against it and take them from the tray.

3122.content: A drone carries things between two storages where no tube reaches.

3128.content: Hold a route card and press Shift + Right-click on the storage to take from, then on the one to carry to: a chest, machine or storage cell.

3129.content: To carry only one thing take it in the other hand and press Right-click in the air with the card: the sample is written down.

3130.content: Place the drone nest, give it energy, press Right-click on it and put the card in: one for Mk1, up to four for Mk4.

3131.content: Look in the panel: “ready”, “in flight” or why it stays.

3132.content: Reach of the storages from the nest: 16, 24, 32, 48 blocks; load 8, 16, 32, 64 things; endurance 160, 260, 400, 640 blocks a charge.

3133.content: It takes from a chest through its bottom side and puts in through its top: a furnace gives its result and takes its raw. Takes only what the second one has room for.

3134.content: It flies straight or in an arch up to 12 blocks high over an obstacle; needs a free block over each storage (or beside).

3135.content: “Put in a route card with both ends written” — the card has only one end: finish it on the second storage.

3136.content: “Nothing to carry” — the first is empty, or the second has no room, or nothing matches the sample.

3137.content: “A point on the card is too far” — move the nest closer or raise its version.

3138.content: “No way through: blocks are in the path” — blocks stand in the way: open the top of both storages.

3143.content: Jumps you between your bases inside one world.

3150.content: Place one jump beacon at each base and give both energy. Leave two free blocks above each.

3151.content: Stand on the beacon and press Right-click on it: the list of beacons shows the price and the time of charging.

3152.content: Choose the second one and stand still on the beacon: step off and the jump is canceled.

3153.content: Name it: press “Rename” in its panel, or press Right-click on it with a name tag; a beacon named on an anvil keeps the name when broken.

3154.content: Right-click on the beacon — the list of destinations

3155.content: Shift + Right-click — its panel: energy, cards, guests

3156.content: Range: 400, 1,500 and 6,000 blocks; Mk4 reaches the whole world. Price: 200 ⚡ plus 2 ⚡ per block, so a long jump needs an Expander card: a Mk4 holds 32,000 ⚡.

3157.content: Charging takes 3–8 seconds by distance, less in higher versions and with Accelerators.

3158.content: Only you and what you wear travel: no mounts. Between worlds it does not jump — there are gates, rockets and ships. Others see your beacon only if you open “Guests”.

3159.content: “Not enough charge” — the number says how much is needed; add energy or a higher version.

3160.content: “There is no room above that beacon” — free two blocks over it.

3161.content: “The far side does not answer” — its place did not load in time: try again.

3166.content: A cabin that carries you and others between floors.

3173.content: Dig a shaft 3×3 and place the lift drive at its foot, in the wall, facing into the shaft: the cabin rides in the 3×3 square in front of it.

3174.content: Stack lift guide rails on top of the drive, one column: the cabin rises as many blocks as the column is high.

3175.content: At each floor put a lift call post within five blocks of the middle of the shaft, at the height of that floor. The lowest floor is at the drive.

3176.content: Give the drive energy and press Right-click on a post: the cabin comes. Name floors with a name tag: press Right-click on the post with it.

3177.content: Step into the cabin and choose: Space — a floor up, Shift — a floor down, Right-click on the floor of the cabin — the list of floors.

3178.content: Space / Shift in the cabin — a floor up / down

3179.content: Shift in a cabin that stands without power — slow descent to the next floor

3180.content: Shift + Right-click on a post — the list of floors

3181.content: Speed 2.5, 4, 6, 9 blocks a second by version; height 24, 48, 96, 192 blocks (the Field Amplifier adds a quarter each). 10 ⚡ per block.

3182.content: Calls wait in a queue, the cabin stands two seconds at each floor. Any redstone signal on the drive keeps the next calls waiting.

3183.content: “No shaft nearby” — the post stands farther than five blocks from the middle, or below or above the shaft.

3184.content: “Rails do not reach this floor” — extend the column of rails.

3185.content: The cabin stands between floors — no power: give it energy and it goes on, or press Shift to descend.

3190.content: Carries things between chests and machines in capsules through tubes.

3196.content: Place one pneumatic station right against a chest and another against the second one. Join them with pneumatic tubes.

3197.content: Give both energy: a beam or a battery beside.

3198.content: Press Right-click on the first and switch “Mode” to “Sending”. The second stays “Receiving”.

3199.content: Put up to five samples into the filter sockets: the sender sends only what matches them, the receiver takes only that. Empty — everything.

3200.content: For a storage: “On request” beside it, then in the storage window Ctrl-click (Cmd on a Mac) sends a stack to the chosen station.

3201.content: A station looks into its chests every 2, 1, 0.5 or 0.25 seconds by version; capsules fly 8, 12, 16 or 24 blocks a second and carry up to a stack.

3202.content: A capsule costs 16 ⚡ and half a ⚡ per block of the way.

3203.content: A capsule flies only if there is room at the far end. Where it goes: highest priority (0–9, set in the panel), then with a filter, then nearest.

3204.content: Tubes branch freely, up to 4,096 blocks. Two stations touching each other without a tube are not joined.

3205.content: “No tube to another station” — the tubes do not reach another station: look for a gap.

3206.content: “No one to send to” — nobody takes this: check the filter and the mode of the second one.

3207.content: Red lamp and steam — the receiver has no room, even in its tray: empty the chest behind it.

3208.content: The station sees only what touches it: move it against the chest with any free face.

3214.content: A crafting grid in the storage window: parts come from the storage.

3219.content: Make the Crafting Grid card and put it into the sockets of the terminal panel: press “Panel” in the storage window.

3220.content: Return with “Storage window”: a 3×3 grid has appeared on the right.

3221.content: Lay the parts out and take the result: what was used is refilled from the storage. Shift on the result crafts many.

3222.content: With JEI or REI press “+” beside a recipe: the parts go into the grid from the storage and your inventory, Shift — for as many crafts as there are.

3223.content: “Grid to storage” puts the grid back; closing the window does too.

3224.content: One Shift click crafts at most 64 times. A recipe that needs an analysis or a blueprint works only for those who know it.

3225.content: A part is red or missing — the grid is filled in part: put the rest in by hand.

3226.content: No grid — the card lies in the terminal of another base, or it is not in a socket.

3231.content: All your things in one window with search and sorting.

3238.content: Place a storage terminal and put storage cells right against it and against each other — any face will do, in any shape.

3239.content: Give the terminal energy: a beam or a battery beside it. Cells need none. Press Right-click on it to open the storage window.

3240.content: Store: Shift-click things in your inventory or put a stack into the window. A cell also has a slot of its own, and a hopper can feed it.

3241.content: Take: click a thing — a stack, the other mouse button — half, Shift — straight into the inventory. Use the search bar to find it.

3242.content: Tab — to the search bar and out of it

3243.content: Search: part of a name, @mod or #tag

3244.content: Esc — clear the search, then close the window

3245.content: A cell holds, by version: 4,096 things of 12 kinds, 8,192 of 24, 16,384 of 36, 32,768 of 48. The Expander card adds half.

3246.content: A terminal sees 12, 24, 48 or 96 cells by version; the Field Amplifier adds a quarter each. Without a terminal a group still works with 12 cells.

3247.content: A broken cell keeps its contents in its item; place it to get them back. Filled cells do not stack.

3248.content: “No energy” — the terminal starts with 40 ⚡: lead a beam to it.

3249.content: A cell is not in the storage — it does not touch the rest, or there are more than the terminal sees.

3250.content: Does not go in — all kinds are used or no room: add a cell or a higher version.

3257.content: Stores spare energy and gives it back; charges portable batteries for rockets.

3263.content: Place the block beside a generator or machine, or link it with a beam. The gauge on its side shows the charge.

3264.content: For more, stack eight blocks of one version into a cube 2×2×2: with the last one they grow together into a big battery. A cube of 27 (3×3×3) becomes a huge one.

3265.content: To charge portable batteries put flat ones into the upper slot of the panel and take charged ones out. The lower pair does the opposite: pours a charged one into the block.

3267.content: A big battery holds and gives as much as 10 blocks, a huge one as much as 40: more than the blocks it is made of.

3268.content: A portable battery takes 8,000 ⚡; the block fills one a second.

3269.content: Two batteries touching each other even out their charge. To send it one way only, set the sides.

3270.content: The cube did not grow together — all blocks must be of one version and the cube full; another battery inside must fit in it whole.

3271.content: Cards fell out when it grew together — the blocks that became parts give theirs back: put cards into the panel of the whole battery.

3272.content: You broke a block of a big battery — it falls apart, each block keeps an equal share of the charge.

3278.content: Charges portable batteries and the multitool from the sun.

3284.content: Place the station under open sky: nothing above it up to the top.

3285.content: Press Right-click and put up to four flat batteries (or multitools) into the slots, one in each.

3286.content: Wait for the day: panels open and batteries charge one after another, half a minute each. Take the charged ones.

3287.content: Put a charged battery into the rocket’s window, or press Right-click on the rocket with it.

3288.content: Day only; no beams needed. One flight discharges one battery. At night or under a roof charge them in a battery block: 8,000 ⚡ each.

3289.content: Hoppers put flat batteries in and take charged ones out on every side. The village power engineer swaps a flat battery and an emerald for a charged one.

3290.content: “No sunlight” — it is night or something stands above the station.

3291.content: It charges slowly — only one battery is charged at a time: put up a second station or use a battery block.

3298.content: Burns anything a furnace burns and turns it into energy.

3304.content: Place the generator, press Right-click on it and put fuel into the slot: coal, charcoal, wood, a lava bucket.

3305.content: Put a battery or the machine right beside it, or link them with a beam: it burns only while there is somewhere to send the energy.

3306.content: To feed it by itself put a hopper with fuel above or at the side. Below, a hopper takes the empty bucket left from lava.

3307.content: Output: Mk1 10 ⚡ per tick, Mk2 20, Mk3 40, Mk4 80 (20 ticks a second). A piece of coal gives 16,000 ⚡ in any version, only faster.

3308.content: Cards: the Catalyst gets a quarter more out of fuel, the Accelerator burns one and a half times faster (the same energy from a piece).

3309.content: In the Nether a hot throat of a vent mouth beside or below a generator with no fuel feeds it with its breath.

3310.content: It does not burn — its store is full: nothing takes the energy. Or the slot is empty: look at “Fuel” in the panel.

3311.content: The second lava bucket does not go in — take the empty one out of the slot first.

3318.content: A bridge between the beam grid and cables and machines of other mods.

3324.content: Try without it first: put a cable of another mod right against a machine of this mod — machines take energy and generators and batteries give it through any face.

3325.content: Need one clear joint? Place the converter against their cable or machine and link it to your grid with a beam.

3326.content: Press Right-click and choose the direction: “Taking from others” or “Giving to others”.

3327.content: One unit of theirs is one ⚡: Team Reborn Energy on Fabric, the loader’s own energy on NeoForge and Forge.

3328.content: Throughput per tick: Mk1 100 ⚡, Mk2 200, Mk3 400, Mk4 800; the Conductor card passes half as much again. When giving, it pushes energy into the neighbors itself.

3329.content: “No energy mods in the game” — no mod with energy is installed: there is nothing to join.

3330.content: Nothing passes — the direction is wrong, or that face is closed for energy in “Sides”.

3335.content: Two dusts from one raw ore; glass, salt and fuel from the rock of other worlds.

3341.content: Place the crusher, give it energy and put raw ore into the upper slot of its panel (not the ore block: mine it first).

3342.content: Take the two dusts out of the tray and smelt each in any furnace: two ingots instead of one.

3343.content: To run by itself put a hopper with ore above and a hopper with a chest below.

3344.content: Raw ores: iron, copper, gold, dense iron, adamant, lead, ilmenite, iridium, verdigris, wraith iron — two dusts each.

3345.content: Rock of worlds: impact glass → 2 optical glass, scorched crust → 2 cinder briquettes, sulfur crust → 2 sulfur, hematite gravel → 2 raw iron, methane ice → 2 methane crystals, fire opal → 3 amethyst shards.

3346.content: Cobblestone → gravel → sand, sandstone → 4 sand, bone → 5 bone meal, blaze rod → 4 powder. Spare parts give back part of their metal, no more than half.

3347.content: Raw materials of other mods with the tag `c:raw_materials/…` crush into two of that metal’s dust, if some mod has the dust. All recipes are in JEI or REI.

3348.content: One raw ore or rock takes 2,560 ⚡ and 8 seconds in Mk1, 4 in Mk2, 2 in Mk3, 1 in Mk4; a spare part takes two to four times as much.

3349.content: “The tray is full: take the result” — the tray holds another thing or is full: empty it.

3350.content: “This cannot be crushed: take it out” — this has no crushing recipe; an ore block goes in only as raw ore.

3357.content: Turns ice and magma cream into coolant, the fuel of the diving bell.

3363.content: Place it and give it energy. Put ice, packed ice or blue ice into the first slot and magma cream into the second.

3364.content: For canisters put empty ones into their slot; for the bell lead fuel pipes to a launch gantry at the winch.

3365.content: Make magma cream in a melt pump from lava, or the game’s way: slimeball and blaze powder.

3366.content: Ice gives 125 units, packed ice 500, blue ice 2,000; a magma cream binds 1,000 — a canister. So a blue ice block is two canisters and two magma creams.

3367.content: A canister takes 2,400 ⚡ and 10 seconds in Mk1, 1.25 in Mk4. The tank holds four canisters for Mk1 and 32 for Mk4.

3368.content: It stands with ice inside — there is no magma cream in the second slot.

3369.content: It stands with a full tank — take canisters out, put empty ones in or lead pipes.

3375.content: Smelts everything a furnace smelts, twice as fast and without coal.

3381.content: Place it and bring energy: a battery or generator right beside it, or a beam.

3382.content: Open the panel and put in what to smelt; the result comes out on the right.

3383.content: For automation put a hopper with ore above it and an empty hopper below.

3384.content: One item costs 2,000 ⚡ in any version: Mk2 is twice as fast as Mk1, Mk4 eight times.

3385.content: Takes two cards that suit it: the Accelerator (faster, more energy) and the Economizer.

3386.content: It stands — nothing to smelt, the output is full or there is no energy: the nameplate tells which.

3390.content: Carries energy between two bases at any distance, even between worlds.

3396.content: Craft a pair: the recipe gives two. Place one at each base.

3397.content: Link each of them to its own grid with a beam: press Right-click with the fork on a machine or battery, then on the resonator.

3398.content: Press Right-click with the fork on one entangled resonator, travel to the other end with the same fork and press it on the second one.

3399.content: A double helix of light rises from each end: sparks go up where energy leaves and come down where it arrives.

3400.content: The pair shares one store of 256,000 ⚡; each end passes up to 1,024 ⚡ per tick and reaches 48 blocks by beam.

3401.content: An end works while its place is loaded. The store is kept: charge at home, travel and take it out there.

3402.content: Energy passes by beams only: touching machines do not share with it.

3403.content: The store is gone — a resonator was broken or entangled anew: the pair fell apart and its store with it.

3404.content: Nothing comes here — the far base puts nothing in: fly there and check its generators.

3409.content: From the first generator to a machine that runs: touching blocks and beams of light.

3416.content: Place a  and a  side by side, face to face: energy flows between them by itself.

3417.content: Press Right-click on the generator and put coal into its slot. The battery’s gauge starts to rise.

3418.content: Place the machine you want to power, for example a crusher, right against the battery — it is already fed.

3419.content: For a machine farther away take a  and press Right-click on the battery: its lens is caught and a ghost beam follows your aim.

3420.content: Press Right-click with the fork on the second machine: the beam lights up. Pulses run along it the way energy flows; a dim beam carries nothing.

3421.content: Too far or behind a corner: put a pole, a resonator, a beam mirror or a prism between them and link piece by piece.

3422.content: Right-click with the fork on two machines — a beam; on the same one again — let the lens go

3423.content: Shift + Right-click with the fork — put out all beams of this block

3424.content: A beam reaches as far as the better of its two lenses: Mk1 24 blocks, Mk2 32, Mk3 40, Mk4 48. A pole and a bushing have no lens of their own: 24, or as far as the other end reaches.

3425.content: A resonator’s crystal sets its range: quartz 24, moonstone 32, fire opal 40, methane ice 48. Press Right-click on it with the crystal; the old one comes back to you.

3426.content: One block holds up to 6 beams; a mirror 2 (reach 16), a prism 4 (reach 12).

3427.content: Glass, ice, panes and bars let a beam through; tinted glass and any other block cut it. To lead it into a sealed room build a lens bushing into the wall: the air stays in.

3428.content: Consumers are fed first, what is left goes into batteries; when the generators fall short, batteries give it back. A consumer does not pass energy on to its neighbor — a battery does.

3429.content: The beam sparks against a block — something stands across it: clear the way, it lights up again within a second.

3430.content: “Too far” — put a pole or a resonator in between, or use a machine of a higher version.

3431.content: “This lens is full” — six beams is the limit: lead the rest through a pole or a prism.

3432.content: Touching, but nothing flows — open “Sides” of both and check that energy is not closed on that face; or a machine is switched off by redstone.

3440.content: Burns Hemera oil to turn raw Thalassian ore into the ore of home you choose.

3446.content: Place it, give it energy and Hemera oil: press Right-click on it with a bucket of the oil, or lead a fuel pipe to it.

3447.content: Put raw ironstone, peacock ore, electrum, pegmatite or pitch shale into the crucible slot.

3448.content: Choose in the panel what to part it into. The choice is remembered for each family. With an empty slot < and > leaf through the families.

3449.content: Take the ore out of the tray and smelt or crush it as usual.

3450.content: Ironstone: iron, nickel, cobalt… Peacock ore: 3 copper, tin, zinc, lead… Electrum: gold, silver, platinum… Pegmatite: gems. Pitch shale: 2 coal, 4 redstone, uranium… Metals of other mods need those mods.

3451.content: Usually one raw for one output; rare ones take more at once: emerald, platinum, uranium 3, diamond and iridium 4.

3452.content: For each raw: 125 units of oil (a bucket is 1,000) and 4,800 ⚡, 10 seconds in Mk1, 1.25 in Mk4. The tank of Mk1 holds four buckets. Fortune does not work here.

3453.content: “Not enough Hemera oil in the tank” — pour in a bucket of Hemera oil: oil seeps ooze out of Thalassia’s ochre basalt.

3454.content: It waits for more raw — the panel says how many this output needs at once.

3455.content: Full tray — another ore lies there: empty it after changing the choice.

3461.content: Stores one liquid fuel and shares it through fuel pipes.

3467.content: Place the depot and join it to the fuel plant with fuel pipes: the plant sends its fuel when it has no canisters.

3468.content: From canisters: press Right-click and put full ones into the first slot; the depot pours them out one after another. It fills empty canisters from the other slot.

3469.content: Lead fuel pipes to the launch gantry beside the rocket, or press Right-click on the depot with an empty bucket: a bucket is a canister.

3470.content: Another fuel: empty the depot to zero, then just pour the new one in, or press “Next fuel”.

3471.content: Holds one of four: rocket fuel, helium-3, liquid pearl, coolant. Capacity 16 canisters for Mk1, 32, 64 and 128 for Mk4. No energy needed.

3472.content: Canisters by hopper: full and empty go in from above and the sides, emptied and filled come out below. Pipes of different fuels never mix.

3473.content: A broken depot keeps the fuel in its item.

3474.content: “Next fuel” is gray — fuel remains: take it with buckets or canisters; less than one goes by “Drain the rest”.

3475.content: The pipe is empty — the fuel of the depot and of what it is joined to differs, or the side is closed.

3482.content: Sets the gravity you choose in a ball around it.

3488.content: Place it in the middle of the room and bring it energy.

3489.content: Press Right-click and set the radius with − and +; “Show the field” draws the ball.

3490.content: Set the strength beside it: 100% is Earth’s gravity.

3491.content: Strength from 25% to 200% in steps of 25; radius from 2 blocks up to 6 (Mk1), 9, 12, 15 (Mk4).

3492.content: Cost per tick: 2 ⚡ × radius × (0.5 + strength): radius 6 at Earth’s gravity is 18 ⚡. At lower strength it is cheaper.

3493.content: You still float — no energy, or you stand outside the ball: turn on the field display.

3498.content: Powers every machine in a ball around it without beams.

3504.content: Place it in the middle of the workshop and bring it energy: a battery beside it or a beam.

3505.content: Press Right-click on it and set the radius with − and +. “Show the field” draws the ball.

3506.content: Look for short arcs: they strike the machines it feeds; their number is in the panel.

3507.content: Radius: Mk1 up to 4 blocks, Mk2 6, Mk3 8, Mk4 10; the Field Amplifier adds a quarter per card. Throughput 120 ⚡ per tick for Mk1, doubling with each version.

3508.content: A quarter of the energy is lost on the way. It feeds only machines that use energy — not batteries, generators or other emitters.

3509.content: A machine is not fed — its center is outside the ball, or the emitter has no energy: at shortage machines are fed in turn.

3514.content: Show what is going on in the beam grid and in the pipes.

3520.content: Hold the multimeter and press Right-click on a machine, pole or resonator of the grid: the answer is a line above the hotbar.

3521.content: Read it: + is what the grid gives a tick, − what it takes, then stored and capacity of its batteries. “Touching” is energy shared with neighbors, “here” — this machine’s own store.

3522.content: Press Right-click with the manometer on a pipe or a machine with a pipe: what flows, how full the system is and how many machines are on it.

3523.content: The grid numbers are the real flow of the last half second.

3524.content: Spare hull plates and copper sheets mend worn gear of the mod: plate in one hand, gear in the other, Right-click — a quarter of its durability for a hull plate, a tenth for a copper sheet.

3525.content: “No beams” — no beam reaches this block.

3526.content: “The pipe is empty: no machine on it” — the pipe is joined to nothing, or the side of the machine is closed.

3531.content: Where each liquid comes from, how to take it and what to do with it.

3536.content: From the world: press Right-click with an empty bucket on a still source block.

3537.content: From a machine: press Right-click with an empty bucket on a fuel plant, depot, pearl liquefier or cryo still that holds at least 1,000 units.

3538.content: Into a machine or vehicle: press Right-click with a full bucket on a depot, gantry, separator or a craft with that fuel. A bucket is one canister.

3539.content: On the ground: press Right-click on a block and the liquid spills; a dispenser does it by redstone.

3540.content: From the world: molten gold — the Forge, tears — the Lament, acid — Venus, liquid methane — Titan, molten iron — the Iron Ocean; tidewater, pitch and tide glow — Thalassia, Hemera oil — its seeps.

3541.content: From machines: rocket fuel and helium-3 — the fuel plant, liquid pearl — the pearl liquefier, coolant — the cryo still.

3542.content: Careful when spilled: gold burns like lava, tears slow and weaken, fuel and Hemera oil flare up from any fire, helium boils away in seconds, pearl throws you aside, coolant freezes, acid burns, pitch holds you.

3543.content: A bucket of Hemera oil burns in a furnace for 32,000 ticks — longer than lava.

3544.content: The bucket does not fill — it is a flow and not a source, or the machine holds less than a bucket.

3545.content: The bucket does not pour in — the machine holds another liquid, its tank is full or it takes no buckets.

3553.content: A higher version works faster and holds more; a card changes one thing.

3559.content: Make the machine core of the next version. Its recipe page says where each part comes from.

3560.content: Break the machine with a pickaxe and put it on the crafting table together with the core. Charge, fluid, cards and sides stay.

3561.content: Place it and put cards into the sockets of its panel: Mk1 has one, Mk2 two, Mk3 three, Mk4 four.

3562.content: Power by version: ×1, ×2, ×4, ×8 — speed, capacity and throughput. The energy per item stays the same.

3563.content: Accelerator (+50% speed, +66% energy): coal generator, electric furnace, crusher, pump, separator, assembler, electrolyzer, bioreactor, dome, blower, suit rack, lab, both gantries, jump beacon, nest, node; lift +25%.

3564.content: Economizer (−16% energy each): everything that spends energy, except the charging gantry, the pearl liquefier and the cryo still.

3565.content: Field Amplifier (+25% reach, +33% energy): dome, gravity generator, scrubber, emitter, storage terminal (cells), lift (height), jump beacon (range), drone nest, cargo node (one chunk).

3566.content: Expander (+50% capacity): every machine. Conductor (+50% throughput): battery, oxygen tank, converter, suit rack, fuel depot, gantries, emitter.

3567.content: Catalyst (+25% yield): coal generator, bioreactor. Membrane (−20% leak): dome, blower. Reflector (+30% light): solar panel. Crafting Grid: storage terminal.

3568.content: The card does not go in — this machine has no work for it, or the socket opens with a higher version.

3569.content: A charge is lost after taking an Expander out — what no longer fits disappears.

3574.content: What every machine has in common: energy, sides, hoppers, redstone, upgrades.

3580.content: Place the machine and press Right-click: its panel opens. The nameplate says whether it works and, if not, why.

3581.content: Give it energy: put a generator or battery right beside it, or link them with a beam — press Right-click with a  on one machine, then on the other.

3582.content: Put materials into the panel by hand, or with hoppers and pipes: from above and the sides in, from below out.

3583.content: To change that, open “Sides” in the panel and set each of the six sides.

3584.content: A beam needs a clear path (glass is fine) and reaches 24 blocks with Mk1 lenses, up to 48 with Mk4; Shift with the fork puts out the beams.

3585.content: Any redstone signal switches a machine off; its panel and the sign above it say so.

3586.content: The next version is crafted from the previous one and a machine core; everything inside stays. Upgrade cards go into sockets of the panel: one for Mk1, one more with each version.

3587.content: No energy — check that the generator burns, the beam is not blocked and the energy side is not closed.

3588.content: Output full — take the result out of the panel or put a hopper below.

3592.content: Draws metal and crystals out of molten seas and lakes.

3598.content: Place the pump on the shore, so that a source block of the melt is right beside it or below it.

3599.content: Give it energy: the panel says it draws from the melt.

3600.content: Take the output from the mold, or put a hopper below. When the sources around run out, move the pump.

3601.content: What it draws: molten gold → 3 gold ingots, living gold → 4 gold ingots, tears → 2 sorrow quartz, pupil glass → 1 lens crystal, lava → 1 magma cream.

3602.content: It reaches the blocks around it — one to each side, diagonals too — on its own level and two below. Each block it has drawn cools into rock.

3603.content: A block takes 9,600 ⚡ and 20 seconds in Mk1, 2.5 seconds in Mk4.

3604.content: “No melt within reach” — only source blocks count, flowing melt does not: move closer.

3605.content: “The mold is full: take the ingots” — the mold holds another thing or is full: gold and quartz do not mix.

3610.content: Melts ender pearls into liquid pearl, the fuel of the rift shuttle.

3616.content: Place it, give it energy and put ender pearls into the feed slot.

3617.content: To get canisters, put empty ones into their slot: each 1,000 units fill one.

3618.content: To feed the shuttle, lead fuel pipes to a launch gantry at the pier; a press with a bucket works too.

3619.content: Two pearls make a canister (1,000 units), so 10 seconds for a canister in Mk1 and 1.25 in Mk4. A canister takes 2,400 ⚡.

3620.content: The tank holds four canisters for Mk1 and 32 for Mk4; when it is full and there are no pipes or canisters the machine stands.

3621.content: Hoppers: pearls and empty canisters from above and the sides, full ones from below.

3622.content: It stands — no pearls, no energy or the tank is full: the nameplate says which.

3628.content: Rocket fuel from coal and helium-3 from regolith. It needs no energy.

3634.content: Place the plant, press Right-click and put empty canisters into their slot.

3635.content: Put coal, charcoal or a coal block for rocket fuel — or moon regolith or a gas giant’s haze for helium-3.

3636.content: Wait ten seconds per canister and take the full ones. Put them into the rocket’s window or press Right-click on the rocket with one.

3637.content: No canisters? Lead a fuel pipe from the plant to a fuel depot or a gantry: the fuel flows there by itself.

3638.content: One canister: 2 coal or charcoal (a coal block counts as 9), or 4 regolith, or 2 blocks of haze.

3639.content: Each slot for canisters holds 16. The tank for pipes holds four canisters and only one fuel at a time.
