3640.content: Hoppers: feed and empty canisters from above and the sides, full ones from below. Fuel technicians in villages sell canisters.

3641.content: “Put in empty canisters or connect a pipe of this fuel” — no empty canister and no pipe of this fuel.

3642.content: The tank still holds the other fuel — take it with a bucket or an empty canister; a rest of less than one goes by “Drain the rest”.

3649.content: Where hoppers, pipes and energy enter and leave a machine, and how to switch it off.

3654.content: Open the panel of the machine and press “Sides”.

3655.content: Choose what you set up: input, canisters, fuel, output, upgrades, fluid or energy — only what this machine has is shown.

3656.content: Click a side: none, input, output, both — in a circle; the other mouse button goes back. Sides are counted from the machine’s front.

3657.content: Turn on pushing (“Does not push output” → the other way): once a second the machine puts its output into the chest or machine beyond an output side.

3658.content: “Copy setup” and “Paste setup” move the setup to another machine.

3659.content: By default: items in from above and the sides, output out from below, fluid and energy through every side. Upgrade cards are closed to hoppers until you open them.

3660.content: Beams of the grid do not look at sides; energy of touching machines and cables of other mods does.

3661.content: Any redstone signal switches a machine off: it neither works nor gives energy. “Redstone switches it off” in the same window makes it deaf to redstone.

3662.content: Break a machine with a pickaxe: its charge, fluid, upgrade cards and side setup stay in the item. Without a pickaxe nothing drops.

3663.content: A hopper does not put in — the slot takes only what suits it, or that side is “none”.

3664.content: The sign of a switched-off machine hovers above it — remove the lever, torch or wire beside it.

3675.content: Place the panel so that nothing stands above it, all the way up: any solid block over it, however high, shades it.

3676.content: Put a battery beside it or link it with a beam: the panel makes nothing at night, the battery carries the base through.

3677.content: Press Right-click on the panel: “Light” shows how much of Earth’s noon falls on it, beside it the output.

3678.content: Output at 100% light, per tick: Mk1 4 ⚡, Mk2 8, Mk3 16, Mk4 32. Each Reflector card adds 30%.

3679.content: Light by world: Mercury 258%, Venus 138%, Earth, the Moon and Thalassia 100%, Mars 66%, Ceres 36%, Jupiter, Europa and Io 19%, Saturn, Titan and Enceladus 10%, Uranus 5%, Neptune 3%.

3680.content: Beyond the rifts and at the bottom of the vents there is no night, but the light is weak: the Facet 50%, the Breath and the Forge 40%, the Hive and the Lament 30%, the Eye 25%, the Mycelium 20%, the Ash 15%; the Nether Sun 100%.

3681.content: In the End and the Nether a panel gives nothing. Rain halves the light.

3682.content: Light 0% — it is night, something stands above, or there is no sky here.

3683.content: Too little far from the Sun — burn coal or bring energy from another world by an entangled pair.

3733.content: The rock under the Nether where the vents glow: the way in, what is there and home.

3738.content: Build the “Salamander” or the “Anvil” (known after the Keeper of Tears of Lament) and fill it with coolant.

3739.content: Fly over the lava sea of the Nether and hold Shift: the ship dives through the lava and comes out under the vault of the Depths.

3740.content: Find floating blocks of basalt and geodes by ,; magma currents carry the ship.

3741.content: Fly into a vent to come out in its world if you have been there.

3742.content: Home: rise to the vault — the ship surfaces from the lava of the Nether.

3743.content: The dive happens only while you hold Shift; the ship must be over the lava sea. Only ships of the depths.

3744.content: The ship does not surface — there is no room up there: move under another place of the vault.

3751.content: Sewn seams, splits with rift goods and the endermen’s gathering.

3756.content: On outer islands beyond the cities look for a narrow dark crack sewn with thread; read the sign in its middle with an empty hand (Right-click).

3757.content: Open with the riftscope the rift under whose side the seam lies: the seam splits apart.

3758.content: Find the split and break it with a pick: a pinch of void shards and something of its world. Then it splits again, nastier: for five minutes it burns whoever stands on it and gives nothing.

3759.content: When endermen gather at a split (once in 4–8 days, three minutes, from the stage “The Rifts Flow”), stay to the end without looking them in the eyes: they leave a block of that world and messengers’ nacre.

3760.content: A split breath burns: Breath’s purple steam needs a helmet, Eye’s blinks and angers endermen. One look — the whole ring is against you.

3761.content: The seam does not open — its rift is not open yet: look at the sky side.

3766.content: How to calm a singing crystal and get a whole fire rose, and where the cold geode is.

3771.content: In the Depths find with , a dark shell two hundred blocks across with glowing seams and fly into the one bright mouth. Walk on its floor.

3772.content: Strike a crystal once: it starts ringing (six beats). Hit it three times in its own beat — the next notes; then it is calm for two minutes.

3773.content: Mine the heart now with a pick: the great fire rose comes out whole.

3774.content: For the cold geode track the Cold Spot in the magmoscope; its seams do not glow. Fit a Heating Unit, not a Cooling Unit.

3775.content: Small crystals ring every 0.8 second, medium 1.1, big 1.5; a hit off beat makes a wave that throws you. A great rose splits into four plain ones; a broken one gives plain roses only.

3776.content: In the geode shelter the heat of the Depths is 15 %. A shadow growth in the cold one crumbles into clots: one clot in a vent ship’s cockpit is three buckets of coolant.

3777.content: “Heart shattered” — the crystal was not calm: three hits in beat first.

3794.content: Vent mouths and the bones of giants in the Nether rock under pressure.

3800.content: In the Nether go to a dull thud and stand on the extinct crust cone: it is a vent mouth. When anyone opens a vent on the server, all mouths heat up and spit embers.

3801.content: Find giant’s remains — arcs of ribs above a mound — in soul sand valleys, basalt deltas or Nether wastes; a vent breach may throw one out beside its new mouth, most often in soul valleys and deltas.

3802.content: Make a  (heatproof lens, copper, blaze rod) and  (gilded slag, blaze rod).

3803.content: Hold the probe and look at rock: dark red spot — pressure 1, orange — 2, shaking whitish — 3, blue — bones. Press Right-click on rock for a reading. It sees four blocks deep.

3804.content: Open pockets of pressure 1 or 2 first: they vent steam and lose a step. Cool deeper ones with the  (place it on the rock, fill it with coolant) or canisters.

3805.content: Take the bone out with the chisel in your hand: it comes whole. A pick shatters it.

3806.content: A pocket of pressure 3 swells white for a second and a half: plug the hole with a block or pour coolant, or lava bursts and cracks bones near (2 blocks).

3807.content: The lance cools a pocket three blocks deep by a step a second: 60 coolant a block. While the Nether sleeps the rock is cold and gives nothing.

3808.content: “Held by cold rock” — the Nether is asleep: open a vent (any player) first.

3809.content: Bone crumbled — use the chisel, not a pick.

3815.content: The void above the End where the rifts hang: the way in, what drifts there and home.

3820.content: Build the “Moth” or “Comb” (plans are known after the Unblinking of the Eye) and fill it with liquid pearl.

3821.content: Take off in the End and climb until the sky ends: the ship comes out above the disk of the End.

3822.content: Fly among islands by the map (F8): currents carry the ship, caches hold plans. Use , for islands and stations.

3823.content: Fly into a rift to enter the sky of its world — only if you have landed there before.

3824.content: To go home fly down to the pale disk of the End under the islands.

3825.content: A current carries faster and for free. In the layer of islands the ship’s speed is tied to loaded chunks.

3826.content: Only ships of the void pass; with any other ship the instruments refuse.

3827.content: The sky does not end — you are in the End with a different ship or not at the top: climb higher.

3828.content: The autopilot stops at an island — steer by hand for the last stretch.

3860.content: Four echoes in the magmoscope and how they lead to the Crucible.

3865.content: After the Depths, use the magmoscope in the Nether and strike the magma: the answer that differs is an anomaly.

3866.content: Fifth Echo: three strikes from different places — the place where the arcs meet. Wandering Heat: lead the crosshair after the spot and hit its fast beat.

3867.content: Heartbeat: strike both halves of its beat, follow the pale waves. Cold Spot: hit in the silent third beat.

3868.content: Each record is a , once a day per anomaly; three on different days and it is traced.

3869.content: Heartbeat leads to the Crucible Threshold: a platform with a golden ring in the Depths. Read its plaque, look at the anvil at the well’s mouth.

3870.content: When the Heartbeat is traced and the Hearth tablet read, strike the anvil with the price: 128 deep embers, 16 suncoal, 8 fire roses.

3871.content: Noticing pays 4 embers, a later record 1, tracing 2. The well leads to the Crucible dungeon.

3872.content: No seismogram — one per anomaly a day: come back after sunrise.

3873.content: The anvil is silent — not traced, not read or the price is short: it shows the ticks.

3903.content: The modules of the dark and fiery far roads: what each tier opens.

3909.content: Spindle Keel I: the  (from the Spinner) with firstshell, condensed void, void thread and a hull armor module. Put it into a void ship.

3910.content: Crucible Jacket I: the  (from the Last Giant) in smoldering obsidian and adamant over the heat shield. Put it into a vent ship.

3911.content: Tier II: the keel takes a nacre navigator (observatory), two sargasso yarn and a ring spark; the jacket — a deep sounder, two hydrous ringwoodite and a ring spark.

3912.content: Tier III: a shadow image and a ring spark; the keel adds a pattern card of the Sampler, the jacket a buried core. The other recipe swaps the far part for more of nearer goods.

3913.content: Warp Thread: the second Spindle, condensed void, firstshell — a weapon that ties foes together. Beat the Spinner again for it.

3914.content: The keel reaches 150, 600, 1,500 threads; the jacket 2,000, 5,000, 6,371 km. Each next tier burns less.

3915.content: The workshop of a station does not raise these tiers — only the crafting recipes do.

3916.content: Tier III keeps the far berth closed — the shadow image must be read.

3920.content: How to dive under the islands of the End, catch finds and build over the void.

3927.content: Open a rift: at the rims of outer islands on its side pale currents rise from the void.

3928.content: Craft a  (void shards, string, ender pearl), press Right-click on a block at the edge: it is the anchor.

3929.content: Jump into the current: it lifts you to the rim and holds. Glide with elytra for height. To take the line off, crouch and press Right-click in the air.

3930.content: Touch finds drifting in it or press Right-click with the  within ten blocks. The deeper, the richer.

3931.content: Press pebbles around a shard into s, press Right-click looking at the void in the End: the plate stands in the air three blocks ahead.

3932.content: Right-click with a  in hand — open it

3933.content: A line of 64 blocks and 4 pulls back from below the world’s bottom (long: 112 and 8; on a plate 1.5 times farther). One pull costs a turn of the spool. Without it the void keeps you.

3934.content: Up to four finds near one diver; a drifting find sinks for good when the current lets go. A new one every 3.5 seconds.

3935.content: No current — the rift of this side is closed, or you are far from an outer island.

3936.content: The line does not hold — press Right-click on a block in the End and keep it in your inventory.

3984.content: Belt ores and the mining beam

3985.content: Ores that no world has hang in space: mine them with a pickaxe or from the cockpit.

3992.content: Fly past Mars to the Main Belt and press ,: for a minute the pulse marks fields and rich rocks.

3993.content: Come to a nickel-iron asteroid. From the cockpit: aim, hold Left Alt — the mining beam digs straight into the hold.

3994.content: On foot: land the ship on the rock with Shift, get out in a whole spacesuit and dig with an iron pickaxe or better.

3995.content: Smelt the raw ore in any furnace into ingots.

3996.content: Hold Left Alt — mining beam (the module must be fitted)

3998.content: Tetrataenite — nickel-iron of the Main Belt; olivine — rare pallasites; osmiridium — red Trojans by Jupiter. Osmiridium needs a diamond pickaxe or beam II.

3999.content: Interrift islands: condensed void and chorus quartz. The Depths: ringwoodite and fire rose in the geodes.

4000.content: Beam I digs like an iron pickaxe, II diamond, III netherite; reach 24 / 32 / 40 blocks; a bucket of fuel lasts 200 seconds. It does not touch chests and machines.

4001.content: The ship is slow in a field — it goes no faster than the terrain loads: that is normal.

4002.content: “The hold is full: the rest falls out” — empty the hold or fit a hold module.

4003.content: The beam does not light — no mining beam in the sockets or the tank is empty.

4009.content: A capital ship that carries your ships, your stores and your base, and comes when called.

4015.content: Get one: answer a distress call in space or buy it at the order board of a station. The key goes into your inventory.

4016.content: In open space press Right-click with the key, or “Call the Freighter” (unbound by default), or the button in the ship console: the freighter jumps to you with its hangar facing you.

4017.content: Fly your ship into the glowing hangar opening on the port side: it docks, you stand on the deck. On foot in a spacesuit you may fly in too.

4018.content: To leave by ship press Right-click on the hangar console; Shift + Right-click picks the next ship. On foot — the airlock, in a spacesuit.

4019.content: To move the freighter itself, press Right-click on the command console on the bridge, choose a body of the system or your ship and press “Jump”.

4021.content: “Call the Freighter” (unbound by default) — call with the key anywhere in the inventory

4022.content: Berths: class C 1, B 2, A 4, S 6. Length about 150, 300, 700, 950 blocks. One freighter per player.

4023.content: It comes to any open space — the Solar System, the Interrift, the Depths, far roads — but not to worlds. Calling is free.

4024.content: Only the owner calls and jumps it. Friends (a list on the command console) dock, walk and build; a ship leaves the hangar only with someone who may fly it.

4025.content: Lost the key — a new one costs 4 of the station’s supply at any order board with freighters.

4026.content: “The hangar is full: launch a ship first” — fly a ship out first.

4027.content: “Too close to a planet or a station for a freighter” — fly away from the planet or the station.

4028.content: “The decks are still being fitted: a moment” — a new freighter’s decks take some seconds: wait.

4035.content: Inside: a hangar, a build hall, a hold in one storage network, crew rooms and a bridge with a view of space.

4041.content: From the hangar follow the light lines in the floor: amber leads to the hangar, white to the tower.

4042.content: Stand in an antigrav shaft and hold Space to go up, Shift to go down.

4043.content: Press Right-click on the chart table of the command deck, or open “Deck map” in the command console, to see where everything is.

4044.content: Put things into the terminal of the hold: its storage cells are one network.

4045.content: Build your base in the hall: machines work there as anywhere, while someone is on the decks.

4046.content: Space up, Shift down — in the shaft

4048.content: There is air and Earth’s gravity. Walls cannot be broken, building is only in the hall; the bunks here set no spawn point.

4049.content: Out only by the hangar console and the airlock: an invisible boundary behind walls and windows holds flight, elytra and pearls, in creative too.

4050.content: Old small decks — they widen by themselves when the owner is online, nobody is aboard and nothing you built is in the way; a message counts what is.

4068.content: Frigates follow your freighter and go on expeditions by themselves, even while you are offline.

4073.content: Hire frigates: the order board of a station, “Freighters & Frigates”, the second tab. Or ask a saved captain for one instead of the freighter.

4074.content: Put rocket fuel canisters into the hold of the freighter or your inventory.

4075.content: On the bridge press Right-click on the command console and open the Fleet tab.

4076.content: Choose a mission and one to four frigates of the specialties it wants: the window counts the chance. Press “Send the expedition”.

4077.content: If the crew asks, decide on the bridge while the expedition is under way; with no answer they play it safe.

4078.content: When they return, step onto the decks: the cargo goes into the hold. Mend damaged frigates with hull plates.

4079.content: Up to 6 frigates, 4 missions a game day, 3 expeditions at once. A mission takes 10–40 minutes and 1–2 canisters per frigate; empty ones come back.

4080.content: Survey wants a Scout, mining an Industrial, trade a Trader, salvage a Support, patrol a Combat frigate. Each missing specialty takes 15% of luck.

4081.content: Hire: C 20 of supply + 12 emeralds, B 36 + 24, A 64 + 44, S 110 + 80; the trust is as for freighters. Experience raises class after 6 and 16 expeditions, up to A.

4082.content: Repair: 4 plates per damage for class C, 2 more per class. Two damages — it waits at home. Only the owner commands the fleet.

4083.content: “The hold is full: the cargo waits” — free the cells and press “Unload to the hold”.

4084.content: “One of the frigates cannot go” — it is away or badly damaged.

4090.content: Every station of a people sells three freighters a day and takes yours in exchange.

4095.content: Land at a station of a people and press Right-click on its order board, then “Freighters & Frigates”.

4096.content: Choose one of three; drag the drawing to turn the hull. A line under the window tells what is missing.

4097.content: Pay with “Buy the freighter”: the freighter stands by the station, the key is in your inventory.

4098.content: With a freighter of your own it is an exchange: wait for the survey of your decks and press “Exchange freighters”.

4099.content: C — 48 of the station’s supply and 32 emeralds, B — 96 and 64, A — 192 and 128, S — 384 and 256; trust makes it cheaper. Paid from your inventory and the hold of the ship on the pad.

4100.content: Trust of the people: C “Acquaintance”, B “Friend”, A “Kin”, S “Sworn”.

4101.content: In an exchange your old freighter counts for half the price of its class. The base stays in place, the hold and ships move, the key is the same.

4102.content: “The decks do not fit — nothing is taken until they do:” — the list counts what is in the way: blocks, creatures, ships, items. Nothing was touched: clear it and come back.

4103.content: “Someone is on the decks: let them leave first” — let everyone leave the decks.

4108.content: Save a freighter from the Drifters — the first one saved becomes yours.

4113.content: Fit a weapon and fly in open space, away from stations, about ten minutes: the instruments catch a distress call.

4114.content: Put the crosshair on the red mark and hold \`, or fly there: the call waits for twenty minutes.

4115.content: Come closer than 220 blocks: Drifters come in waves. Shoot those at the breaches; hide from the hunters behind the hull.

4116.content: Keep an eye on the bar at the top: it is the freighter’s hull. Shoot all of them down before it runs out.

4117.content: Answer the captain with ; and press “Take the freighter”. A missed call repeats every three minutes.

4118.content: Enemies: class C 5, B 7, A 9, S 11, two more for each further pilot; no more than six at once. The first call is always class C, later ones come after an hour of flight.

4119.content: Flight time counts within one session. Not in creative mode, not with a wrecked ship.

4120.content: Everyone who dealt 20 damage gets an offer of their own; it waits three game days. Already have a freighter: exchange it, take a frigate or take thanks in supply and emeralds.

4121.content: No call — a weapon must be fitted; one event at a time in a space, then it rests a day.

4122.content: The freighter jumped blind — its hull gave in: next time start with those at the breaches.

4128.content: A ship from space enters the sky right above it — no more landing thousands of blocks from home.

4135.content: Place the beacon at your base under open sky: it lights itself.

4136.content: Press Right-click on it: the window tells whether it is lit and why not, and who sees it. Type a name there.

4137.content: Came back from space? Near the ball of the world turn the mouse wheel: it chooses a beacon or none.

4138.content: Fly into the ball: the ship comes out right above the chosen beacon.

4139.content: Shift + Right-click on a dark beacon — light it at once

4140.content: Up to four lit beacons per world for each player; only you and your /team see them.

4141.content: Works in worlds ships enter from space, behind rifts and at the bottom of vents: there the shuttle and the bell land beside it. In the Nether it needs 6 free blocks above instead of sky.

4142.content: Without a beacon fly to the mark “Takeoff pad”: the ship enters above it if it came within 1,500 blocks of it.

4143.content: “The beacon needs open sky above it” — remove the roof and press “Light it” in the window.

4144.content: You already have four here — break one of them.

4145.content: Came out elsewhere — “no beacon” was chosen: turn the wheel at the ball.

4151.content: Carries animals, villagers and other creatures between worlds aboard your ship.

4158.content: Fit a Bio Bay into a module socket and land the ship.

4159.content: Lead animals on leads to the ship and press Right-click on the stern hatch: all within 12 blocks walk in, the leads come back.

4160.content: Villagers, traders, golems, hostile mobs: press Right-click on them with a stasis capsule within 24 blocks of the ship. One capsule — one creature.

4161.content: To unload, land, open the console tab “LIVE CARGO” and press “Unload” by a creature.

4162.content: Shift + Right-click on a friend’s ship — its live cargo

4163.content: Places: 6 / 12 / 20. Chicken or wolf 1, sheep, cow or villager 2, horse 4, iron golem 8; bigger ones do not fit. Masters and guardians do not ride.

4164.content: A creature keeps everything: trades, name, owner, age. It survives logging out, jumps and the hangar.

4165.content: The owner and friends of the ship of any level load and unload. The ship must stand: on the ground, on a pad or still in space with no pilot.

4166.content: “There is no air outside” — unload under a dome or in a sealed room, or press again within five seconds to do it anyway.

4167.content: The capsule finds no ship — come closer than 24 blocks to your own or a friend’s ship with a Bio Bay.

4168.content: You boarded instead of the animal — there is no Bio Bay in the ship or the animal is farther than 12 blocks.

4171.content: Friends and crew of a ship

4173.content: The void lance, the slag flak, and flares against torpedoes.

4180.content: Put the void lance into a void ship or the slag flak into a depth ship, as any weapon, and hold Left-click.

4181.content: Put the flare launcher into a module socket of any ship.

4182.content: When the instruments shout “TORPEDO”, press F: the torpedoes chase the flares.

4183.content: Left-click — lance or flak, F — flares

4184.content: Lance: damage 8 / 10 / 12 a second, range 120, goes past shields. Flak: 5 / 6 / 7 to everything within 3–3.5 blocks of the burst, range 64, also shoots torpedoes down.

4185.content: Flares: 2 / 3 / 4 charges, a new one every 20 / 16 / 12 seconds.

4186.content: No flares left — turn sharply or boost: a torpedo turns slower than you. Shoot down the ship that fired — its torpedoes go blind.

4191.content: A piercing slug, homing torpedoes and a shield that takes hits before the hull.

4198.content: Mass driver and torpedo rack go into weapon sockets, the shield into a module socket.

4199.content: Mass driver: hold Left-click — a slug every second and a half goes through everything on the line.

4200.content: Torpedoes: keep torpedo packs in the hold or pockets, bring a target into the frame and press Right-click.

4201.content: Left-click — mass driver, Right-click — torpedo salvo

4202.content: Mass driver: damage 12 / 16 / 20, range 160. Torpedo rack: 2 / 3 / 4 torpedoes of 30 damage, range 200, 3 seconds to reload, one pack per salvo.

4203.content: Shield: 30 / 45 / 60 points; after three seconds without hits it recovers 4 a second. Rockgnawers chew the hull under it.

4204.content: The torpedo rack is made from a Drifter’s tally: shoot down a Drifter ship.

4205.content: No salvo — no target in the frame, no packs, or the freighter key is in your hand: it calls the freighter instead.

4211.content: Flies the ship through space by itself while you walk the deck.

4216.content: In space put the crosshair on a world, a station or a mark and press .: the ship turns and goes there.

4217.content: Or open the map with F8, click a goal and press “Autopilot to the target”.

4218.content: Press ; and walk the deck, or sleep on the bunk; the ship stops before the goal.

4219.content: Take the helm back with any movement key or ..

4220.content: It flies at cruise speed and burns no fuel. With no goal under the crosshair it holds the course of the nose.

4221.content: A world with your landing beacon: the ship stops right above the beacon. Only in space, and not on a towing rope.

4222.content: “The autopilot works in space only” — climb out of the sky first.

4228.content: Calls your ship to you from wherever it stands.

4234.content: Press Right-click on your ship with the beacon in hand: it is tuned and glints.

4235.content: Wherever you are, press Right-click in the air: the ship lifts off and lands within 20 blocks, where the runes glow.

4236.content: From another world or far space wait: the uplink line counts the time.

4237.content: In the same world it costs only the take-off fuel. From another world — the fuel of that flight, at least a quarter of a bucket.

4238.content: Not enough fuel, or the ship is wrecked — a tug brings it for the supply of its road: 6 per missing bucket, at least 8. A wreck arrives wrecked.

4239.content: An occupied ship does not come, and a ship comes only where its road leads. The beacon recharges for 30 seconds.

4240.content: A lost beacon is no loss: press Right-click in the air with a new one — it finds your last ship.

4241.content: “Someone is in a seat” — let everyone leave the ship and its deck.

4245.content: Friends and crew of a ship

4247.content: C → B → A → S: every class makes the same ship better in everything.

4253.content: Gather the price of the next class in your inventory: the supply of the ship’s road and substances of its belts.

4254.content: At your shipyard: land the ship on the slipway, press Right-click on the console and press “Raise the class”.

4255.content: Or at a station of the peoples: land on a marked pad, press Right-click on the dock console, first “Refuel and repair”, then raise the class.

4256.content: Each class: speed +12%, hull, hold and jump +25%, scanner about +10%, one more module socket. The hull is made whole.

4257.content: Starships: B — 64 stardust, 8 tetrataenite ingots; A — 128 stardust, 4 pallasite olivine, 8 osmiridium ingots; S — a master’s heart, a comet core, 4 black diamonds, 64 stardust.

4258.content: Void ships: B — 64 void shards, 8 condensed void; A — 128 shards, 4 chorus quartz, 8 hive amber; S — a heart of the road, 8 firstshell plating, 4 lens crystals, 64 shards.

4259.content: Depth ships: B — 64 deep embers, 8 fire roses; A — 128 embers, 4 ringwoodite, 8 sorrow quartz; S — a heart of the road, a nether star, 4 sorrow quartz, 64 embers.

4260.content: Class S is raised only for those whom at least one people of that space calls “Kin”: orders of the station boards earn trust.

4261.content: “Refuel and repair first” — a dock raises only a whole ship with a full tank; the shipyard takes any.

4264.content: Belt ores and the mining beam

4267.content: One window for the hold, modules, fuel, repair, friends and live cargo of a ship.

4273.content: Open it: press E in the seat, or stand by the ship, hold Shift and press Right-click.

4274.content: Put buckets or canisters of the ship’s fuel into the fuel slot: they pour in one by one, the empties come back.

4275.content: Put metals of the ship’s road into the repair slot — or press Right-click on the hull with them. A wrecked ship needs a hull section there first.

4276.content: Press “Inventory” at the top for your own inventory — armor and crafting — without leaving the seat.

4277.content: If your freighter key is in your inventory and you are in open space, press “Call the freighter”.

4279.content: “Call the Freighter” (unbound by default) — call the freighter (set the key in Controls)

4280.content: The console is for the owner and the First Mate; a passenger or pilot gets the ordinary inventory on E.

4281.content: Repair: starships — titanium, lead, iridium, hull plates, polymer; void ships — shulker chitin and shells, resonant shards, drone wax, end stone; depth ships — adamant, dense ingots, wraith iron, verdigris, basalt scutes.

4282.content: A hull section raises a wreck to a quarter of its hull. Anyone may refuel and repair anyone’s ship.

4283.content: The console does not open — it is someone else’s ship: ask the owner for the First Mate level.

4284.content: No freighter button — you have no freighter yet; it is gray — the tooltip tells why.

4287.content: Friends and crew of a ship

4289.content: Friends and crew of a ship

4290.content: Lets other players aboard, to the helm or to the console — even while you are offline.

4295.content: Open the console of your ship and the tab “SHIP FRIENDS”.

4296.content: Click a player’s row to make them a friend; click again to remove. Type a nick to filter, the wheel scrolls the list.

4297.content: Click the label at the right of the row to change the level: Friend → Passenger → Pilot → First Mate.

4298.content: Use the top rows for everyone at once: “Everyone” and your /team. The friend is told their new level.

4299.content: Friend: loads and unloads live cargo, takes the wreck into a hold and crosses over without asking.

4300.content: Passenger: also boards by the hatch and sits in a seat without you.

4301.content: Pilot: also flies, jumps, uses the autopilot, the call beacon and dock services. No console, no hold.

4302.content: First Mate: everything you can — console, hold, hangar, upgrades — except taking the ship apart and changing these rights.

4303.content: A stranger boards by the stern hatch while the owner is aboard, and rides in a free seat while the owner flies. Rights belong to one ship; the freighter has its own list on the bridge.

4304.content: No such tab — only the owner sees it: the First Mate cannot change rights.

4305.content: The click does nothing — stay within 12 blocks of the ship or sit in it.

4306.content: A one-seat ship has no place for a passenger — board by the stern hatch and walk the deck.

4312.content: Every ship has an interior you can walk while it flies.

4318.content: From the seat press ;: in space at any moment, above a world only when landed. The ship brakes or goes on by autopilot.

4319.content: From the ground press Right-click on the stern of a landed ship: the hatch lets you in.

4320.content: Press Right-click on the things aboard: pilot seat — back to the cockpit; cargo hold — the ship’s hold; chart table — where you fly and how long.

4321.content: On a long autopilot flight press Right-click on the bunk: when everyone aboard is asleep, the ship is five seconds from the goal.

4322.content: Leave by the hatch with Right-click when the ship stands on the ground or on a station pad.

4323.content: ; — from the seat to the deck

4324.content: The only ways out are the hatch and the pilot seat: an invisible boundary around the walls and windows holds even in creative mode, with elytra or pearls.

4325.content: In open space the hatch leads only to another ship within 16 blocks, by the light sleeve. Modules are fitted in the console, the rack only shows them.

4326.content: The bunk works with at least half a minute left and nobody in the seats. The hold aboard is for the owner and the First Mate.

4327.content: “Open space is behind the hatch. Leave through the pilot seat” — return to the pilot seat.

4328.content: “Land first, or go to space: without a pilot the ship would fall” — land, or rise to space.

4329.content: “You cannot fall asleep while the crew is awake” — everyone aboard must lie down.

4332.content: Friends and crew of a ship

4335.content: Take off, leave the sky for open space, land — and what each key of the cockpit does.

4341.content: Fill the tank: press Right-click on the ship with a bucket or canister of its road’s fuel — helium-3, liquid pearl or coolant.

4342.content: Press Right-click on the nose to take the pilot’s seat; on the stern hatch — to board the deck.

4343.content: Hold Space to rise, W for thrust and climb: the instruments on the right count the blocks left to space. At the top the shutter closes and the ship comes out in open space.

4344.content: In space the ship coasts on its own. Aim at the ball of a world and fly into it: the shutter closes again and you are in its sky.

4345.content: Hold Shift to go down; on the ground press Shift again to get out.

4346.content: W thrust, S brake, A D — sideways

4348.content: E — ship console: hold, modules, fuel, hull

4351.content: Hold Left Alt — mining beam, F10 — marks on the sky

4352.content: Take-off, boost and jumps burn fuel; cruising is free even with an empty tank.

4353.content: A ship enters only the sky of a world where you have already landed by rocket, shuttle or bell.

4354.content: The ball remembers where you took off: fly to the “Takeoff pad” mark, or put up a  at the base and choose it with the wheel near the ball.

4355.content: “No fuel for take-off” — get out and pour in a bucket or canister.

4356.content: Came back far from home — you touched the ball in another place: use the take-off mark or a landing beacon.

4357.content: The hull is wrecked — press Right-click on the ship with a ; metals of its road mend scratches.

4362.content: Crosses thousands of blocks in four seconds.

4368.content: In space put the crosshair on a world, station or scanner mark farther than 1,500 blocks — or choose it on the map (F8) and press “Set as target”.

4369.content: Hold \` for a second and a half until the drive is charged.

4370.content: The ship comes out beside the target, moving toward it: brake with S or turn away.

4371.content: One bucket of fuel for every 20,000 blocks.

4372.content: Range depends on the hull — 40,000 for the first scout — and grows with class and the jump module. A far goal is several jumps in a row.

4373.content: You did not arrive — the jump is shorter than the distance: jump again.

4374.content: No charge — the target is nearer than 1,500 blocks: fly there or use the autopilot.

4378.content: Modules make a ship faster, tougher and roomier; each kind has three tiers.

4384.content: Craft a module: tier I from metals of the road, II from belt ores, III from rare finds of space. The recipe is under its name in the journal.

4385.content: Open the ship console and put it into a free module socket; take it out the same way.

4386.content: Hover over a socket: the tooltip tells what it takes and which class opens it.

4387.content: Sockets of class C: scout 2, explorer, fighter and exotic 3, hauler 4; one more per class. Fighters also have 2 weapon sockets. One module of a kind, except holds.

4388.content: Engine: speed ×1.1 / 1.18 / 1.26. Thrusters: turn ×1.12 / 1.22 / 1.32. Armor: hull ×1.3 / 1.6 / 2. Hold: +9 / 13 / 18 cells.

4389.content: Scanner: range ×1.5 / 2 / 3. Tank: ×1.5 / 1.75 / 2. Jump drive: range ×1.5 / 1.75 / 2, fuel ×0.8 / 0.7 / 0.6. Mining beam: 24 / 32 / 40 blocks.

4390.content: Regolith processor: turns regolith and ice of the hold into fuel (asteroid regolith 45 thousandths of a bucket each, comet ice 180), one every 4 seconds at tier I.

4391.content: Any ship flying through the Sun’s corona (350–1,600 blocks above the surface) gathers fuel: 10 to 120 thousandths of a bucket a second, more the deeper; corona scoop ×1.5 / 2 / 3. Keep a third of cruise speed.

4392.content: Heat grows there: at the very edge 100% in 11 seconds, with a heat shield in 18 / 28 / 44. From 100% the hull burns, at 125% a module burns every five seconds. The shield eases star winds too.

4393.content: Weapons, shields, the Bio Bay and star drives have pages of their own.

4394.content: The socket does not take it — the line under the window names the reason: a closed socket, the same kind already fitted, another road.

4395.content: Above a world the ship is no faster — over worlds speed is capped at 30 blocks a second, 45 on boost; in space it is not.

4401.content: Salvage: a ship in the hold

4402.content: The grapple folds an empty ship into your hold. No module is needed.

4407.content: Make room: free cells in the hold — scout 6, fighter 7, exotic 8, explorer 9, hauler 16; Drifter hulls 4–8.

4408.content: Fly closer than 24 blocks, put the ship in the frame at the crosshair and hold Left Alt for six seconds.

4409.content: If it is someone else’s wreck, wait until the owner agrees.

4410.content: To unload, land (or stop in space), open the console and click the ship in the hold list: it appears alongside.

4411.content: Your own ship — always, whole or not; another’s — only wrecked, with the owner’s consent, the owner being online (friends of the ship need no consent). With people aboard it is towed instead.

4412.content: A server may change that rule (rescue rule): consent — as above, the usual one; free — anyone’s wreck is yours to take; own — only your own ships. A tow always asks the people aboard.

4413.content: One ship per carrier, two in a hauler. Each takes 15% of speed and adds half the jump fuel (a hauler carries twice as easily).

4414.content: It keeps class, modules, fuel, hold and owner. The owner may call it out of your hold with a call beacon.

4415.content: A disabled Drifter hull is nobody’s: unload it by your shipyard and there take it apart or press “Refit” to make it your ship.

4416.content: The capture breaks — you were hit, the target left the frame or 24 blocks: match speeds and hold on.

4417.content: “It still flies — disable its engines first” — shoot out its engines first.

4418.content: “Its own hold carries a ship — unload it first” — a ship with a ship inside is not taken.

4424.content: A rope of light drags a ship with people aboard, or one that does not fit your hold.

4430.content: Hold Left Alt on the ship for six seconds, closer than 24 blocks — as for salvage.

4431.content: Wait until the people aboard agree; if it is empty — its owner.

4432.content: Fly: the ship follows 12–16 blocks behind. It jumps with you and goes through the sky with you.

4433.content: Land: the towed ship is set down beside and the rope comes off.

4434.content: Left Alt — let go of the rope, from either ship

4435.content: No boost while towing, a jump costs twice the fuel, and the carrier’s pilot cannot leave for the deck. The rope breaks at 72 blocks.

4436.content: The people on the towed ship walk its deck; its autopilot and jump are off.

4437.content: “No room alongside to set the towed ship down — release the line” — land on open ground.

4439.content: Salvage: a ship in the hold

4442.content: A sleeve of light carries you to another ship in space or on the ground.

4448.content: Come up to the other ship, closer than 16 blocks side to side, and match its speed: the difference is at most 6 blocks a second.

4449.content: Look at it from your seat and press ;.

4450.content: Wait for its pilot or owner to agree (15 seconds). You land in a free seat, or on the deck if there is none.

4451.content: From the deck press Right-click on the hatch: in open space it leads to the nearest ship in reach.

4452.content: To bring in someone floating outside, hold Left Alt on them closer than 24 blocks; they must agree.

4454.content: The owner and friends of that ship (any level) need no permission. Nobody crosses to a ship that jumps or stands in a shipyard’s work.

4455.content: “Match speeds first — the sleeve breaks at more than 6 bl/s” — brake until both stand still to each other.

4456.content: “Nobody to open the hatch” — its owner is not aboard: ask to be made a friend of the ship.

4458.content: Salvage: a ship in the hold

4460.content: Friends and crew of a ship

4462.content: The pulse cannon: a beam that hits where you aim at once.

4469.content: Put the cannon into a weapon socket of the console; a ship without weapon sockets takes one weapon into a module socket.

4470.content: Take off, aim and hold Left-click. A target near the crosshair gets a frame; when the frame is red, the pulses hit it.

4471.content: Watch the arc under the crosshair: fire in bursts shorter than three seconds.

4473.content: Ctrl — boost in bursts to dodge

4474.content: Damage 3 / 4 / 5, range 96 blocks, 6 pulses a second; three seconds of fire overheat it for two. Two cannons fire in turn.

4475.content: Each pulse burns a little fuel: a bucket is about 3,300 pulses. Rocks crack too, but most of their ore is lost: mine with the beam.

4476.content: Only in flight, from the pilot’s seat.

4477.content: “CANNON IS DRY” — the tank is empty.

4478.content: The socket refuses the weapon — fighters take it only into weapon sockets.

4484.content: The shipyard builds ships, raises their class and takes them apart.

4490.content: Place the console facing you; behind it, on the same level, lay a slipway of 9×5 slipway plates: the console stands at the middle of the long side.

4491.content: On the plates put two towers of four crane sections: on the far left and the near right corner, as seen from the console.

4492.content: Press Right-click on the console: lights mark the missing blocks; when all is in place, the shipyard lights up. It needs no energy.

4493.content: Make the parts the window lists — hull sections, main drives, a cockpit, a ship core — and keep them in your inventory.

4494.content: Press Right-click, choose a ship and press “Build”: the cranes weld it in 45–120 seconds. The tank is empty: refuel it with a bucket or a canister.

4495.content: To take a ship apart, land it on the slipway and hold “Take apart (hold)”: modules, hold and parts go to the store of the shipyard, fuel into your empty buckets.

4496.content: A scout is known after the first master of its road: the Terminator Warden (Swift), the Mother of the Comb (Moth), the Giant’s Remnant (Salamander).

4497.content: A hauler — after the last master: the Abyssal Gale, the Unblinking, the Keeper of Tears. Other ships need a blueprint from caches and wrecks of the belts or from stations: hold it and press Right-click.

4498.content: Only the owner takes a ship apart, with nobody in it and no ship in its hold. Part of the hull sections and drives comes back; what fuel does not fit is lost.

4499.content: “The shipyard is not assembled” — the message counts missing blocks: check the towers stand on the plates and on the right corners.

4500.content: “No blueprint. This form is built from a blueprint found in space caches and stations” — you need that ship’s blueprint.

4501.content: “The slipway is busy” — fly the ship off the slipway or wait until the cranes finish.

4507.content: A view from above on the space you are in: worlds, belts, stations and your finds.

4513.content: Press F8 in the cockpit, on the deck or on foot in space.

4514.content: Zoom with the wheel, drag to move; “To the ship” and “Whole system” bring the view back.

4515.content: Click a goal and press “Set as target”: it stays marked in the sky. Then hold \` to jump or start the autopilot.

4516.content: Press , in flight to add fields, caches, rich rocks, wrecks and stations to the map.

4517.content: F10 — marks in the sky: all, important, none

4518.content: The map knows only what you found with instruments and the scanner. The scanner pulses every 8 seconds; range depends on the ship.

4519.content: The goal is closer than 1,500 blocks — no jump there: fly or use the autopilot.

4523.content: Belt ores and the mining beam

4525.content: Remains of old expeditions: a chest, a story, and sometimes a ship you can raise.

4530.content: In the belts or on the night side of a planet press ,: a wreck is marked on the sky.

4531.content: Come closer than 420 blocks and pulse again: the ship is identified, the journal gets a record and you get stardust.

4532.content: Get out in a spacesuit, take the chest of the hold: the crew journal, modules, parts, sometimes a blueprint.

4533.content: In a scout’s wreck look for a glowing core. With 2 hull sections and a main drive in your inventory press Right-click on it: a Swift and its blueprint are yours. Place the ship with Right-click on the ground.

4534.content: One wreck by every planet and the Moon; in the Main Belt and the Trojans one in every second square of 4,096 blocks, elsewhere rarer. Solar System only.

4535.content: A core raises a ship once.

4536.content: “Parts needed” — the message names what is missing from your inventory.

4538.content: Belt ores and the mining beam

4541.content: Phenomena of space: how to notice, visit and study them, and which are dangerous.

4546.content: In space keep the crosshair on a trembling patch of stars or a strange point until it is noted. Some are found from the ground: reflector, astrograph, graviscope — the codex tab says which.

4547.content: Open the journal’s “Anomalies” tab: each page says what to do, what is dangerous and which jump opens.

4548.content: Aim at its mark and hold \`; on the place press , from five different sides: five pieces of data and it is studied.

4549.content: Coronal ejection and gamma burst: instruments count down — fly behind a planet or moon until it passes. A merger: start a jump on a wave crest — it is free.

4550.content: Pays: noticed 4 stardust, visited 12, each piece of data 1, studied 4.

4551.content: Solar corona heats the hull: at 100 % it burns, at 125 % modules burn. A dark cloud hides lumps: , shows them for three seconds.

4552.content: Nothing on the map — it passes by schedule: track it with the telescope the codex names.

4582.content: How to catch a comet and get ice and a comet core.

4587.content: Wait for the comet: an announcement comes every two to four days, it is in the sky for twenty minutes.

4588.content: In space aim at its mark and hold \`: you come out three to five hundred blocks from the core. Fly closer than 64 blocks.

4589.content: Hold Left Alt on the crust and ice. Near the core the ship keeps pace by itself. Deep in the big lump is the heart — one comet core a comet.

4590.content: Use , near the core: the heart and the vents show for a minute, once per comet it pays stardust.

4591.content: Vents on the sunny side wake up: the instruments warn just before a jet hits.

4592.content: The mark is off the comet — it moves: jump again and fly to the fresh mark.

4593.content: “The comet has gone: the order is closed” — the comet left.

4596.content: Belt ores and the mining beam

4675.content: An emitter on the ground sends a seed into orbit, and the core of your station gathers there from light.

4681.content: Choose a world: any planet of the Solar System from Mercury to Neptune, the Moon, Earth, or a world beyond a rift or a vent. Open sky above the spot is required.

4682.content: Put the  on the ground, lay a 7×7 square of  around it (48) and set a column of three  on each corner plate (12). Missing blocks show as ghosts.

4683.content: Press Right-click on the heart, bring what it asks — a , 64 stardust, 16 tetrataenite ingots and materials of this world — and press “Give what I carry”.

4684.content: Hold “Hold to launch”, step away: ten seconds of charge, then the beam. Half a minute later the core is in orbit.

4685.content: Stand still on the heart for a second: the beam lifts you to the station. The lift pad in the hall takes you back.

4686.content: Aim at a round plug in the hall wall with a module kit in hand and press Right-click: the module builds itself outside. Start with the Dock.

4687.content: One emitter and one station per player in each world; eight places in orbit for everyone (two at a rift or a vent).

4688.content: Inside there is air and Earth gravity; the shell does not break. Crouch and press Right-click on a plug with an empty hand — the station console: parts, name and team.

4689.content: A broken heart gives back what was given; smashing the bowl before the flash cancels the launch, the cargo stays.

4690.content: In the Interrift and the Depths the launch burns islands out of a harbor 112 blocks around, but not those with player buildings.

4691.content: “The sky above the heart must be open” — clear everything above the heart; in worlds without sky light 32 blocks of emptiness are enough.

4692.content: The beam does not lift — stand in the middle and do not move; someone else’s beam carries only its owner and guests beside him.

4693.content: “The station is still building” — wait until the previous part is finished.

4694.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4699.content: A tiny sun from the observatory: it feeds a station of level “Ring”.

4705.content: Record the Orion Nebula with an astrograph and a photo plate, fly there with the interstellar drive.

4706.content: There take a  out of the core of a proplyd; four pieces of primordial matter come from Arrokoth beyond Pluto.

4707.content: In the observatory of your station start the project “Pocket Sun”: 60 minutes.

4708.content: Craft it by the opened recipe and put it into the station hold: the Ring tier asks for it.

4709.content: The station-ring with the pocket sun does all its work 25 % faster.

4710.content: The recipe does not craft — the project is not finished for you: open the observatory console.

4715.content: A race around a station through twelve rings of light.

4720.content: Take “Ring Race” at the order board of a station and take off.

4721.content: Fly through the brightest ring above the station: the clock starts there.

4722.content: Follow the beam from each ring to the next. Finish twelve in a minute and a half.

4723.content: Land and turn the race in at the same board: the first one gives a .

4724.content: A missed ring costs 5 seconds. Time is up — fly through the first ring again; the order stays.

4725.content: The course changes every day. A station record pays 6 trust at once.

4726.content: The clock does not start — only the first ring starts it; fly through the middle.

4727.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4731.content: Creatures of open space, the Interrift and the Depths: where they live, what they do to a ship and what they leave.

4736.content: Look for flickering lights among the stars: a herd takes shape within 150 blocks. Come closer than 48, or catch it with ,, and it counts as met.

4737.content: Belts and Trojans — dust rays: they part before the nose and keep beside a ship up to 94 blocks a second. Mercury and Venus — sail moths. Kuiper belt — ice jellies: keep 11 blocks away from a flaring one.

4738.content: Interrift: hold the ship below 40 blocks a second within 40 blocks of skein weavers and follow them to a cache; below 20 near runaway drones — they mend up to 12 hull and leave wax.

4739.content: Pass within 7 blocks of a ripe chorus drifter in a current: it throws the ship 48 blocks ahead. A void eel waits by dark islands and rifts and drinks the tank: let it go at over 80 blocks a second or in a current.

4740.content: Depths: do not fly through fire bubbles on the currents — they burst in a chain; pop them with the beam from afar. Struck obsidian lets out mites that steal cargo: keep over 38 blocks a second for a second and a half.

4741.content: Before flying to a cache mark look at it: the angler’s false one breathes about twice slower, unevenly, with an orange glow inside. It strikes within 26 blocks, then hides.

4742.content: Rocks of nickel-iron and tetrataenite ore hide rockgnawers; ember, plain and crying obsidian — mites. A mite shot down gives the stolen thing back.

4743.content: The Interrift also has void whales, which sail beside a ship, and facet pikes in ambush at facet islands.

4744.content: The weavers scattered, the drones were blown off — the ship went over 60 blocks a second.

4750.content: How Drifters appear, how to aim, and how to take one of their ships whole.

4757.content: Fit a gun module and fly near asteroid belts or between stations, at least 400 blocks from any station. An ambush comes at once; before a raid the instruments count down 20 seconds.

4758.content: Aim at a ship and press Left-click. Red means the aim is out of reach; overheated guns wait. Keep turning: a ship flying across the fire is hard to hit.

4759.content: To take it whole, hit the glowing engine cells at the stern with the pulse gun; an orange bar under the hull shows them. The crew leaves in a pod, the hull drifts on.

4760.content: Take the hull with the mining beam into your hold within six minutes. At the shipyard it is taken apart or refitted into your ship.

4761.content: A shot-down one scatters plating: fly through the gold mark of the wreck to take your share.

4763.content: Right-click — torpedo at the target in the frame

4765.content: Ctrl — burst of speed: 1.5 s, then 3.5 s to recharge

4766.content: No more than six Drifters near one player. Unarmed ships are left alone. At a quarter of hull they flee with what they have.

4767.content: A share of the loot goes to every pilot who did at least a tenth of the hull’s damage; it lies in the wreck for three minutes (22 blocks to take).

4768.content: Railgun and torpedoes always hit the hull and leave no trophy. Guardians of the lair and the Ark cannot be taken.

4769.content: Nothing happens — the gun burns fuel: the tank is empty.

4770.content: Torpedoes do not fire — put the target in the frame and keep torpedo packs in the hold or inventory.

4771.content: The mark says “taken” — another pilot disabled the hull: only those who fought may take it.

4776.content: Salvage: a ship in the hold

4778.content: Hungry rockgnawers catch ships that loiter among asteroids: how to shake them off or shoot them.

4783.content: In the main belt or a cluster don’t crawl: a swarm notices a ship slower than 40 blocks a second.

4784.content: Red arrows point at the hunters. Shoot them with Left-click; the ones on the nose sit in the crosshair.

4785.content: Use Ctrl and full speed for a second and a half: they fall off. Out of the field the ship leaves them behind.

4786.content: Three to five; each eats one hull a second while it sits. Five minutes of rest after a swarm.

4787.content: A killed one sometimes leaves a tooth.

4788.content: They keep coming back — leave the field, not just turn.
