4811.content: Natives who move into your station and help its work.

4817.content: Become Kin of a people (420 trust).

4818.content: Build the Crew Quarters module on a station of level “Station” or higher.

4819.content: Make a  and press Right-click with it on any native of that people — in a village or on their station. That one stays; another comes to you.

4820.content: Press Right-click on the watch board in the quarters: who lives here and what each gives.

4821.content: One native of each people; places: station 2, citadel 6, ring 10.

4822.content: Greenhouse: Fruiting Folk ×2, Cloud Dwellers +25 %. Refinery: Ring Keepers +25 %. Workshop: Giantkin ×1.5 hours, Facetkin upgrades −25 %. Forge: Gilded −20 % materials.

4823.content: All work: Belt Riders +10 % (twice at Jupiter). Drones: Windbearers carry ×1.5, half the risk. Storehouse: Comb Keepers — two more holds (crouch at the console).

4824.content: “Not yet one of their own” — the contract works only from Kin.

4825.content: No free berth — the quarters are full or there are none on your stations.

4826.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4831.content: Takes off a module, the lowest tier or the whole station and gives everything back.

4836.content: Stand aboard, crouch and press Right-click on a plug or hatch with an empty hand: the station console opens.

4837.content: Choose a part on the left and press “Estimate”: it shows what returns and what is in the way.

4838.content: Remove what is in the way — people, ships, animals, foreign blocks, missing blocks, things in chests and tanks — and ask again.

4839.content: Hold “Hold: dismantle”; for the whole station type its name first. The countdown is 5 seconds for a part and 10 for the station.

4840.content: Stay aboard until zero: leave, log out or lose the right and nothing is touched. Everyone aboard is moved to the emitter or home.

4841.content: Returned: kits whole, the growth materials and the launch cargo of a core; storage, forge, drones, contracts, rations and fuel come as items. Only the 64 supply burned by the launch is lost.

4842.content: The whole station is taken apart only by its owner; a module or tier — also by a teammate with the Dismantling right. The estimate holds for 60 seconds.

4843.content: Bag too full for the return — free the slots the refusal names. Burned islands of a harbor do not grow back.

4844.content: “The estimate is out of date: ask for a new one” — ask for the estimate again.

4845.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4849.content: Each tier adds four sockets and room for more modules.

4855.content: Earn the trust the plan asks for (see the conditions) with peoples that can move in as crew.

4856.content: Make the  and put the materials of the level into your inventory or the station hold.

4857.content: Press Right-click with the kit on any plug of the hall or the hatch in its floor: a new drum grows below, a shaft with a ladder opens to it.

4858.content: Station: 16 osmiridium plates, 8 pallasite lenses and one people that calls you Acquaintance.

4859.content: Citadel: 32 plates, 4 comet cores and two peoples that call you Friend.

4860.content: Ring: 16 light-catcher panels, 8 comet cores, a pocket sun and three peoples that call you Kin. A rim grows around the core.

4861.content: Modules held: outpost 3, station 6, citadel 10, ring 14.

4862.content: A refusal names how many peoples, or what materials, are missing.

4863.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4869.content: What each module of your station does and how its console is used.

4875.content: Dock: land inside the field and press Right-click on the console — the station refuels the ship from its tanks and mends it with repair hours for free.

4876.content: Hangar: press Right-click on its console twice — the first press says what will happen, the second, within six seconds, stores the ship from the pad or brings one out. Crouch to choose another berth.

4877.content: Refinery: press Right-click on the console with comet ice, crystals, asteroid regolith or coal in hand; the tanks fill at a bucket per ten seconds.

4878.content: Workshop: press Right-click on the console with a ship module in hand — the next tier for 24 supply of the road; it also saves repair hours.

4879.content: Greenhouse: press Right-click on the console for rations — one a minute; it also feeds everyone aboard. Crops on its beds grow three times faster.

4880.content: Cabin: press Right-click on the bunk once — you will wake up there. Storehouse: the console opens the hold of 54 cells.

4881.content: Observatory: the telescope needs neither night nor clear weather; press Right-click on the console to survey the sky for new anomalies and to open research projects.

4882.content: One module of each kind. The Orbital Yard, Workshop, Crew Quarters, Drone Bay, Zero-G Forge, Ringwoodite Still and Geodynamo need the level “Station”.

4883.content: Stocks: tanks 24 buckets, 60 repair hours (one per ten seconds), 12 rations. They grow by the clock even without you.

4884.content: Only the owner and the team use module consoles; up to eight players in the team.

4885.content: “Not your station: ask the owner to add you to the team” — the owner adds you in the console (crouch, Right-click on a plug with an empty hand).

4886.content: The workshop refuses a module — interstellar drive, keel and jacket tiers come only from their own recipes.

4887.content: A ship does not come to the station when called — there is no Dock.

4888.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4896.content: Paid work from the order board: supply of the road, emeralds and the trust of the people.

4902.content: Press Right-click on the  by the dock and take an order. You may hold three at once.

4903.content: Ore, Hunt, Comet Ice: bring the named things in your inventory. Hunt asks for rockgnawer teeth or , or trophies of that road.

4904.content: Parcel: land first — the board loads the box into your ship on the pad. Hand it to the board of the named station within ten minutes.

4905.content: Survey: fly to the mark and press , within 160 blocks of it, then come back to the board.

4906.content: Rescue: fly up to the stranded shuttle (24 blocks) with 4 hull plates and a canister of rocket fuel in your inventory.

4907.content: Convoy: meet the cargo drone at its mark, stay within 160 blocks of it and shoot down two waves of Drifters on the way to the buoy.

4908.content: Open the board of the same station again and turn the order in; a parcel — at its destination.

4910.content: F8 — goals on the system map

4911.content: One order of each kind a day per station; a big weekly order is done once in seven days.

4912.content: Survey opens for an Acquaintance; Rescue, Convoy and the weekly order — for a Friend. Comet Ice is there only while a comet is in the sky.

4913.content: A parcel that is late loses 10 trust; a convoy shot down or left — 6. Every fifth Hunt also pays a tier I ship module.

4914.content: “Not done yet” — the thing is not done yet: check the mark in F7.

4915.content: The rescue shuttle flies no closer — it is refused without all the plates and the fuel canister in your own inventory.

4916.content: The convoy drone stands still — you are too far: it waits a minute, then turns home.

4917.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4923.content: Anomaly data and samples turn into new recipes: ship modules, the pocket sun, the magnetic shield.

4928.content: Build the Observatory module on your station and press Right-click on its console.

4929.content: Choose a project: the window shows which data (anomalies in your codex) and samples are missing and where to get them.

4930.content: Bring the samples in your inventory or the station hold and start it. Projects go one after another by real time, even while you are away.

4931.content: Come back online: the finished project opens its recipe for you and the whole team.

4932.content: 10–60 real minutes each. Queue: outpost 2, station 3, citadel 4, ring 5. Canceling returns the samples, not the time.

4933.content: Only the owner and the team start projects. A crafter block does not make recipes from projects.

4934.content: Data are short — visit the named anomaly and pulse the scanner from different sides.

4940.content: Cargo drones carry what your station makes to the peoples and bring emeralds and supply.

4946.content: Build the Drone Bay (level “Station”) and at least one of the Refinery and the Greenhouse.

4947.content: Press Right-click on the route board with a  in hand: the drone takes a route to the nearest people’s station that knows you (Acquaintance).

4948.content: Come back after twenty minutes and press Right-click on the board with an empty hand: the pay is yours.

4949.content: A trip takes up to 4 buckets of fuel and 8 rations; pay is counted from what it carried.

4950.content: One trip in ten is intercepted: half the cargo is lost. Routes: station 1, citadel 2, ring 3.

4951.content: The Light-Catcher module makes all work of the station 25 % faster, at Mercury and Venus — by half.

4952.content: “Nothing to carry: drones take road fuel from the refinery and rations from the greenhouse” — fill the tanks of the refinery or wait for rations: a flight needs two units of cargo.

4953.content: The drone waits — no station of a people that knows you in this space, or all already have routes.

4958.content: How peoples start to trust you, what each step opens and how to get the key of a station vault.

4963.content: Press Right-click on the keeper of a station — the craft that lives only there — and take their errand: ore, a delivery, a comet, a wreck to scan, a ship class.

4964.content: Do the errands in turn and turn each in to the same keeper: every one pays 40 trust.

4965.content: Between errands turn in board orders (9–48 trust each) and tasks of the people’s villages (18).

4966.content: Become a Friend: only then does the keeper trust you with the last errand, the one that pays with the vault key.

4967.content: Press Right-click on the  with the key in your inventory: the key is spent, the loot flies out to you.

4968.content: Steps: Acquaintance 60, Friend 180, Kin 420, Sworn 720 points. Each people counts its own.

4969.content: The dock is 20 % cheaper from Acquaintance and 30 % from Kin; traders — 10, 20 and 30 %.

4970.content: Kin: crew for your station, class S. Sworn: the great gift of the people on the board — its power stays even if the thing is lost.

4971.content: Also: an ancient tablet shown to an elder 9, a master of space defeated 60. Striking one of the people — minus 30.

4972.content: Each vault opens once for every player.

4973.content: The keeper gives no last errand — you are not a Friend yet: the board shows the points.

4974.content: “Sealed” on the vault — it names the key and whom to ask.

4975.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

4980.content: Where a ship is refueled, mended and raised in class away from home, and where pilots trade.

4985.content: In open space press ,: the pulse marks stations from ten times farther than ore. Each hangs by its people’s world: in the Solar System on the sunny side, in the Interrift by a rift, in the Depths by a vent.

4986.content: Put the crosshair on the mark and press .: the autopilot stops before the mouth and then brings the ship over the pad. Among islands and rocks it halts at the first one — fly the last stretch yourself.

4987.content: Hold Shift to sit down on the pad, then Shift to get out: inside there is air.

4988.content: Press Right-click on the  by the pad and choose “Refuel and repair” or “Raise the class”.

4989.content: Walk inside: traders sell fuel, plating and ship modules, the keeper gives errands, the order board stands by the dock.

4990.content: Service costs 3 of the road’s supply (stardust, void shards or deep embers) per bucket of fuel and 1 per 5 hull; a wrecked ship adds 16.

4991.content: A class costs the same as at a shipyard and is raised only for a whole ship with a full tank. Class S needs “Kin” with at least one people of that space.

4992.content: The first visit pays 12 supply, and the station becomes a jump target. The blocks of a station do not break.

4993.content: “No ship of yours on the pad” — land on the marked pad; the dock serves your own ship or one where you have the Pilot right.

4994.content: The ship hangs beside the pad — another ship is on it: wait or land on the deck next to it.

4995.content: The ship stays before the mouth — the pad is taken and there is no free deck beside it: fly in by hand.

4996.content: Guide: Peoples’ stations, orders and trust

5004.content: How to leave the ship in zero gravity, move there and come back alive.

5011.content: Make one or more suit modules: MMU Pack, Mag Boots, Safety Tether — and fit them into the chestplate at a suit rack. The chestplate has four sockets; air and charge need theirs too.

5012.content: Charge and fill the suit, put on all four parts, stop the ship and press Shift: the first press warns, the second within three seconds lets you out.

5013.content: With the MMU Pack move with W S A D where you look, Space and Shift — up and down. Let go of the keys and it holds you in place.

5014.content: With Mag Boots step onto metal — a station hull, an iron asteroid, a ship, the Visitor — and walk; Space lets go.

5015.content: To return, fly up to the ship and press Right-click on its nose.

5016.content: Ctrl — faster flight of the MMU Pack

5017.content: Zero gravity is open space of the mod: the pull is a tenth of Earth’s, so without the pack you slowly sink. Below the block layer the void kills, as in any world — only a ship may go there.

5018.content: The pack takes 1 charge a tick only while its nozzles work. The tether hooks to the ship you left, pulls beyond 32 blocks and snaps beyond 96 or when the ship jumps.

5019.content: On your own station and in a gravity generator’s field weight is normal.

5020.content: The pack does nothing — no charge in the suit or you are not in zero gravity.

5021.content: You fall away from the ship — put a tether on before stepping out, or Mag Boots on the hull.

5022.content: Boots do not hold — they need metal within a block and a quarter under you; a comet core does not count.

5026.content: Suit modules: which for which world

5029.content: Forges the gear of the stars and the armor of the roads from metals floating in a chamber.

5036.content: Build the Zero-G Forge module on a station of level “Station”.

5037.content: Press Right-click on its console or on the chamber: the book on the left lists every recipe with materials and what you lack.

5038.content: Click a recipe: its materials move from your inventory into the four cells.

5039.content: Press “Forge” and wait — it goes on without you. Take the thing from the finished cell.

5040.content: Hold G over a piece of star gear — its power and numbers

5041.content: Star gear of the Solar road needs materials of the belts; Crab and Cygnus X-1 give neutron dust and disk plasma; road armor is of materials of the Interrift or of the Depths.

5042.content: One forging at a time per station. A Gilded master in the crew takes a fifth off every material.

5043.content: Only the owner and the team may open it. Some recipes need a blueprint — the book names it.

5044.content: “Not enough for this recipe: laid out what you have” — bring the rest and click the recipe again.

5045.content: “Ready: take it from the output” — empty the finished cell.

5046.content: Guide: Zero-G Forge and star gear

5052.content: The journal keeps your path: what to do next, how it is done, and everything you have found.

5059.content: Hold the journal and press Right-click. Glowing cyan seals are goals you can do now, gold ones are done, dim ones with a lock wait for the stages before them.

5060.content: Click a seal: its page opens on the right — the task, how to use the thing, its recipe and a scheme of what is built from blocks. Scroll the page with the wheel. The chapters are listed on the left; the line under the title leads to your current goal.

5061.content: Click a part in a recipe to see its own recipe, all the way down to raw materials; “Back” returns.

5062.content: Start typing to search the whole journal, or open the Manual tab for pages about machines and instruments.

5063.content: M — the path on the whole screen and back

5064.content: Hold G over an item in any window — how to use it

5065.content: F7 — your tasks from the natives

5066.content: Records live in your memory, not in the book: a lost journal is crafted again and opens on the same page — the stage you looked at last, in this world.

5067.content: Progress is your own. To bring a friend up to date, hold a  with the journal in the other hand, press Right-click and give them the copy; it costs stardust.

5068.content: A stage is gray — its page lists the stages it waits for.

5072.content: Optical parts: every telescope and many instruments start with a polished lens.

5077.content: Mix glass blend from sand, an amethyst shard and clay at the crafting table.

5078.content: Smelt the blend into  in any furnace.

5079.content: Lay four pieces of glass in a ring for a .

5080.content: Put the blank,  and any wool together: the lens is polished.

5081.content: A refractor needs two lenses — one for the tube and one for the eyepiece — so eight pieces of glass.

5082.content: Guide: The telescope and the sky

5085.content: Decorative blocks for a telescope house.

5090.content: Craft star tiles: eight polished deepslate around stardust — eight tiles.

5091.content: Put tiles into a stonecutter: panels, slabs, stairs, columns, cornices, moldings, beams and the mosaics come out of them.

5092.content: For a starry sky panel lay eight tiles around stardust; a stonecutter carves the constellations out of it.

5093.content: Lamps: moonstone with gold nuggets and glass or tiles. Observatory glass: eight glass around a gold ingot.

5094.content: Every world also has its own building set, statue and stained glass: polished rock, bricks, slabs, stairs and walls come from the same stonecutter. All of it is in the decor tab of creative mode.

5095.content: Columns and beams are placed along an axis, mosaics join with their neighbors.

5096.content: Guide: The telescope and the sky

5099.content: The first telescope: the Moon, Mars and the brightest constellations.

5103.content: Make copper sheets, then tubes and gears from them.

5104.content: Build the four parts: tube, eyepiece, swivel head and tripod. Click a part in the recipe of the journal page to see how.

5105.content: Put them together and place the telescope on the ground with nothing above it.

5106.content: At night press Right-click on it.

5107.content: Guide: The telescope and the sky

5111.content: The sky itself changes while you look: turn your head, join stars into constellations and focus on planets.

5117.content: Place a telescope under open sky, wait for a clear night and press Right-click on it. Goals of this telescope are listed at the edge of the screen.

5118.content: Stars of one color usually belong to one constellation. Aim at a star and press Left-click, then at the next one: a correct line stays, a wrong one goes out.

5119.content: A “star” that does not twinkle is a planet. Zoom in with the wheel, keep the crosshair on it and hold Left-click until it is sharp (about a second and a half).

5120.content: A finished constellation or planet goes into the journal and opens the next stages.

5121.content: Left-click — pick a star; hold on a planet — focus

5123.content: H — ask for one missing line for stardust (offered when you are stuck)

5125.content: Works only at night, in clear weather and under open sky; one observer per telescope.

5126.content: Stardust: Left-click on a shooting star (one every fifteen seconds), and every find pays some. A line costs 2 in the first chapter, more in later ones.

5127.content: A stronger telescope sees everything the weaker one does; what is under your feet is not in the sky, so from the Moon look for Earth.

5128.content: “Needs open sky” — remove what stands above the telescope; glass does not block it.

5129.content: “Too bright” or “clouds” — wait for night or for the rain to end.

5130.content: The figure does not close — real figures have closed shapes: the bowl of the Dipper has four sides.

5131.content: Guide: The telescope and the sky

5135.content: Charges the batteries of a rocket on its table straight from the grid.

5141.content: Assemble the rocket and place the gantry within five blocks of it.

5142.content: Bring it energy: a beam or a battery beside it.

5143.content: Wait while the cable charges the rocket: 8,000 ⚡ for each battery, one a second in Mk1.

5144.content: Mk1 holds two batteries’ worth (16,000 ⚡) and takes 400 ⚡ per tick from the grid: if the grid is weak, it charges slower.

5145.content: It charges rockets only: the shuttle’s thread and the bell’s chain are put in by hand.

5146.content: “No assembled craft nearby” — assemble the rocket or come closer.

5147.content: It does not charge — it needs 8,000 ⚡ in its own store at once: check the beam.

5153.content: Dives from the Nether through lava to four worlds at the bottom of the vents; the winch hauls it home for free.

5160.content: In the Nether find a lava lake and press Right-click with the bell skirt on the lava at least one block from its edge: the skirt floats on top.

5161.content: On the skirt stack the dome, the crown and the winch on top. The last block assembles the bell.

5162.content: Pour in coolant: press Right-click with a canister or a bucket; the cryo still makes it from ice and magma cream.

5163.content: Put in an ember-tempered chain the same way: an iron chain and a deep ember.

5164.content: Fit the module of the world you want on a socket of the dome: press Right-click with it in hand.

5165.content: Press Right-click, then “Climb in”, choose a world on the vent map and press “DIVE”.

5166.content: To go home, board it there, choose the Nether and press “HAUL UP”: no coolant and no chain are needed.

5167.content: Shift — leave the bell before the dive

5168.content: The Forge: 3 coolant, no module. The Ash: 5, heat belt. The Mycelium: 5, slag jacket. The Lament: 7, damper. The tank holds 10 canisters, 3 chains, the dome 4 modules.

5169.content: Under the bell: nothing but air down to the lava, no more than 8 blocks, and 3×3 of lava. Each dive from the Nether takes one chain.

5170.content: A world opens after its vent is found in the magmascope. Where your landing beacon is lit, the bell comes down beside it, otherwise where it stood before.

5171.content: “No lava under the bell: it needs a three-by-three lava pool below” — the lake is too small here, or a block hangs between the bell and the lava.

5172.content: “No winch above the bell” — put the winch back right above the crown.

5173.content: “No chain: put an ember-tempered chain into the bell” — every dive eats a chain: temper another.

5178.content: Fills a rocket, shuttle or bell by hose, straight from fuel pipes.

5184.content: Assemble the rocket on its launch table and place the gantry beside the table — up to five blocks away.

5185.content: Lead fuel pipes from the fuel plant or a depot to the gantry. It needs no energy.

5186.content: Wait: the hose reaches for the rocket and fills a canister a second (Mk1). The panel shows how many are in the tank.

5187.content: A shuttle or a bell is filled the same way: liquid pearl or coolant in the pipes.

5188.content: It looks for an assembled craft up to five blocks to each side, six below and twelve above, and takes the nearest.

5189.content: The fuel it calls for is the rocket’s. With another rocket the old rest goes back down the pipes; if nothing takes it, it waits in the gantry. The tank holds 4 canisters for Mk1, 32 for Mk4.

5190.content: With nothing to fill it acts as a small depot: other gantries, an empty bucket and pipes of other mods take the rest from it.

5191.content: “No assembled craft nearby” — assemble the rocket or come closer.

5192.content: It does not fill — the pipes carry another fuel: a lunar rocket takes rocket fuel, a heavy one helium-3.

5199.content: Goes from the End through open rifts into four worlds and comes home by its thread for free.

5206.content: In the End, under open sky, lay a pier of 3×3 void plating.

5207.content: On the middle plate stack: keel, thread reel, hull, cabin, needle. The last block assembles the shuttle.

5208.content: Pour in liquid pearl: press Right-click with a canister or a bucket; the pearl liquefier makes it from ender pearls.

5209.content: Put in a spool of rift thread the same way: string, popped chorus fruit and a void shard.

5210.content: Fit the module of the world you want on a hull socket: press Right-click with it in hand.

5211.content: Press Right-click, then “Board”, choose a world on the rift map and press “CAST OFF”.

5212.content: To go home, board it there and choose the End: no pearl and no thread are needed.

5213.content: Shift — leave the cabin before the start

5214.content: The Facet: 3 pearls, no module. The Breath: 5, glass armor. The Hive: 5, mirror boards. The Eye: 7, eyelid. The tank holds 10 canisters, the reel 3 spools, the hull 3 modules.

5215.content: Each way out takes one spool. From one world to another costs the sum of both — often more than the tank: go through the End.

5216.content: A world opens after its rift is opened in the riftscope. In a world with your lit landing beacon the shuttle lands beside it, otherwise where it stood before.

5217.content: “No dock under the shuttle: it needs nine void plating blocks” — put back the missing plates under it.

5218.content: “The craft needs a module for this world: see the journal” — fit the module named on the map.

5219.content: “Something is in the way above the shuttle” — clear the sky above it.

5225.content: A rocket is built block by block on a launch table; each next one flies farther.

5231.content: Choose a spot with nothing above it up to the sky and lay a table of launch pad plates: 3×3 for the lunar and interplanetary rockets, 5×5 for the heavy and deep space ones.

5232.content: Stack the rocket on the middle plate from the bottom up by the scheme of its stage in the journal; “Show in world” marks every block.

5233.content: Lunar: engine, 2 fuel tanks, instrument bay, cabin, nose cone, and 4 stabilizers around the engine.

5234.content: Interplanetary: engine, 3 tanks, heat shield, instrument bay, cabin, nose cone; on two sides boosters 3 high, on the other two a stabilizer.

5235.content: Heavy: fusion engine, 4 helium-3 tanks, heat shield, 2 instrument bays, cabin, nose cone; boosters 4 high on all four sides.

5236.content: Deep space: fusion engine, 5 helium-3 tanks, heat shield, 2 habitat modules, instrument bay, cabin, nose cone; at each corner fusion engine, 3 tanks, shield.

5237.content: The last block assembles the rocket. Refuel it: press Right-click on any part with a canister, a bucket or a charged battery in hand.

5238.content: Press Right-click with an empty hand, open the star map with “Board”, choose a world and launch.

5239.content: Lunar and interplanetary rockets burn rocket fuel (10 and 20 canisters), heavy and deep space ones helium-3 (28 and 40). A bucket is one canister.

5240.content: One way from Earth: Moon 4, Venus 7, Mars 8 · Mercury 10, Jupiter 12 · Saturn 14, Uranus 16, Neptune 18. Between two other worlds — the sum of both. Every flight also takes one battery.

5241.content: A rocket lands where you last stood with one in that world. Away from Earth it takes off only with a return stage — or when taken apart and rebuilt on a table there.

5242.content: Break any part — the rocket falls back into blocks; the fuel and the charge are lost, the modules and the cargo stay in the cabin.

5243.content: It does not assemble — press Right-click on the cabin with an empty hand: white marks show the missing blocks.

5244.content: “Something is in the way above the rocket” — clear everything above the rocket up to the sky, 3×3.

5245.content: “This rocket runs on another fuel” — the message names the right canister.

5250.content: Modules go into sockets on the hull and decide whether you can come back.

5256.content: Take a module in hand and press Right-click on a socket of the assembled rocket: the sockets are at the tanks, on the sides of the hull.

5257.content: Missed? Free sockets flash on the hull: press Right-click on a flash.

5258.content: To take a module off, hold Shift and press Right-click on its socket with an empty hand.

5259.content: For a first trip with a way back fit the landing legs and a return stage.

5260.content: Sockets: lunar 2, interplanetary 3, heavy 4, deep space 6, shuttle 3, bell 4. The shuttle and the bell take only the cargo bay and the passenger seat from here.

5261.content: Landing legs — the whole rocket lands. Without them the stages burn up and only the cabin lands, with an empty tank.

5262.content: Return stage — takes off from bare ground, no table needed.

5263.content: Extra tank: half again as much fuel. Kick stage: the way is 20% cheaper, two — 40%, no more than half. Battery pack: 2 more batteries.

5264.content: Solar array: a battery every 30 seconds of daylight under open sky. Life support: air within 8 blocks of the landed rocket while it has charge.

5265.content: Cargo bay: 9 cells. Passenger seat: one more person. Surface scanner: after landing the chat tells where the nearest settlement is.

5266.content: Only the cabin landed — press Right-click on it: modules and cargo are inside. Take them out, rebuild the rocket on a table.

5267.content: “No launch pad here. Fit a return stage, or break the rocket and rebuild it on a pad” — there is no table here: fit a return stage.

5268.content: A friend cannot get in — the seat opens only during the four-second countdown: press Right-click on the rocket then.

5273.content: A ground vehicle for other worlds: seats, cargo, air around it; folds into a pocket capsule.

5280.content: Place the rover bay with at least three free blocks in front of its face. It needs no energy.

5281.content: Press Right-click on it: a chassis in the middle, up to four modules around, a charged battery beside.

5282.content: Press “Assemble”: in three seconds the rover stands three blocks ahead and is yours.

5283.content: Press Right-click on the rover to take a seat and drive.

5284.content: In the seat press E: the panel has the battery slot, modules and the trunk. Put charged batteries in: they fill the charge and come out empty.

5285.content: Hull damaged? Put hull plates into the Repair socket of the panel, or press Right-click on the rover with a plate: each mends 4 of the hull.

5286.content: Done with it? Press “Fold up” in the panel: the rover with everything inside becomes a capsule. Press Right-click with the capsule on open ground to unfold it.

5287.content: W throttle, S brake and reverse, A D steer

5288.content: Ctrl — a quarter faster, Space — handbrake and drift

5290.content: Shift + Right-click on the rover — the panel from outside

5291.content: Crab: 2 seats, 2 modules, 16,000 ⚡. Mule: 4 seats, 4 modules, 9 cells of its own, 32,000 ⚡. Ray: 3 seats, 3 modules, 40,000 ⚡, glides over lava, acid and water; has no tires.

5292.content: A battery gives 8,000 ⚡, a new rover without one has 2,000. A block of road costs 3 ⚡ for the Crab, 4.5 for the Mule, 6 for the Ray. Without charge it does not move.

5293.content: Modules: trunk — 9 more cells (Mule 18); dome — air, warmth and acid cover within 6 blocks (30 ⚡ a second); suspension — 2-block steps, no loss on sand and snow; headlights.

5294.content: Vein scanner — ore marks within 24 blocks every 10 seconds (150 ⚡); turret — 5 damage to hostile creatures in sight within 14 blocks (40 ⚡ a shot); solar panel — 60 ⚡ a second in daylight.

5295.content: The owner and the owner’s /team drive and open the panel; others ride along. Only creatures, blasts and lava hurt the hull; a wrecked rover drops as a capsule with everything in it and a quarter of the hull.

5296.content: “No room in front of the bay” — clear the place three blocks ahead of the bay.

5297.content: It crawls and skids — acid has eaten the tires: press Right-click with a tire repair kit; one kit mends half.

5298.content: It sparks and smokes — the hull is low: mend it with hull plates (a whole one takes 10 for the Crab, 18 for the Mule, 13 for the Ray). The tire kit does not mend the hull.

5299.content: It fell into the void — the capsule with everything lies at the last solid place, the owner is told where. It neither burns nor vanishes; with no such place it goes to the owner.

5300.content: Lava or water — wheels burn in lava and crawl in water: take the Ray there.

5301.content: Modules are left in the bay — the chassis has fewer sockets than you put in.

5306.content: From the cockpit of a rocket you choose a world on the star map and launch.

5312.content: Press Right-click on the assembled rocket: its window opens. Put fuel canisters and a  into the slots.

5313.content: Fit the modules: press Right-click on a socket of the hull with a module in hand.

5314.content: Put on the whole spacesuit, filled with oxygen, and press “Board”.

5315.content: Click a world on the map: on the right are distance, gravity, the price in fuel and what will be left for the way back.

5316.content: Press “LAUNCH”. The sky above the rocket must be open.

5318.content: Only worlds you found in a telescope can be chosen, and each needs a rocket of its tier.

5319.content: Every flight empties one battery and burns fuel; without  only the cockpit lands, with an empty tank.

5320.content: To take off from another world you need a launch table there or a return stage module.

5321.content: “This world has not been found yet. Look for it through a telescope” — the world is not in your journal yet.

5322.content: “No power: put in a charged battery” — charge a battery at a charging station in daylight or in a battery block.

5326.content: Food and plants of the worlds

5327.content: Plants and beasts of a world give food that helps to live in it: warmth, coolness, acid resistance, air.

5332.content: Gather fruits of wild plants. Plant a fruit on the ground of its world (on Earth — only in a hydroponic bed).

5333.content: Wait: the crop ripens in four stages and needs no air, light or dome; bone meal adds a stage. On a hydroponic bed it is five times faster.

5334.content: Kill beasts for raw meat and fry it in a furnace, smoker or over a campfire.

5335.content: Craft dishes at a table from food of one world; buy seeds and food from its herders.

5336.content: Dishes last with the effects in the tooltip: Warmth and Coolness hold cold and heat of the world, Acid Ward its acid, Air Reserve gives a little air without a tank.

5337.content: A crop that has ripened gives its fruit; leave it if you want to plant the next.

5338.content: It will not be planted — the ground is of another world: stand it on that world’s soil or a hydroponic bed.

5342.content: Dungeons: what each one is about

5343.content: Every big dungeon has one mechanism of its own on all its floors; a change is seen and heard 3–6 seconds ahead.

5348.content: Wait by the door for one turn of the cycle: see where it warns, what it does and for how long. Then go — it repeats. Some wait for your hand, not for the clock.

5349.content: Moon — leap shafts; a dust fall darkens the hall for 8–11 s. Mercury — a beam of sun sets on fire for 5 s: keep to the shadow. Venus — acid floods the bottom for 12–14 s: be on the upper tier.

5350.content: Mars — press Right-click on the winch: 4 s later rust-crowned grates rise and pale ones drop for 15 s; again — 15 s more. Jupiter — lightning opens shutters for 8 s, the floor arcs. Saturn — a turn lasts 17 s, gates shut.

5351.content: Uranus — gravity goes into a wall for 3.5 s: jump and you fall sideways; rough floor and crouching hold you, ice does not. Neptune — Right-click on a kingston floods the room for 36 s, again drains it.

5352.content: Facet — Right-click takes the light from its cradle (45 s in hands, a blow knocks it out); in a setting it burns 25 s and opens the veils of its color. Hive — heat melts the wax for 6 s: walk through, it hardens behind.

5353.content: Eye — do not stand in the square 6 s while it watches (invisible is safe; red vessels are blind spots). Breath — a gust lasts 3–3.5 s: one step behind a solid block or crouching. Forge — gold fills the launder 9–14 s; a fresh cast bridge burns 3 s.

5354.content: Ash — while the giant breathes in (6–10 s) stand still or creep. Mycelium — a cloud of 12–16 s eats your air: a lamp or torch in either hand shows the clean thread. Lament — a step of tears for every 3 s you look the statue in the face.

5355.content: A mechanism runs only while someone is near and goes back when everyone leaves; it is one for all players. New rooms stand only in dungeons made after the update.

5356.content: A grate or shutter waits until you are clear of it, and what it can shut has a way out: a winch on its own, a veil that lets out but never in, a ladder in the pit.

5357.content: In the Crucible trip hammers strike 3 s after they groan; in the Loom a needle eye (Right-click) stitches you through a wall to the one that faces the other way, up to 24 blocks.

5358.content: The winch, kingston or cradle does nothing — press Right-click: the line above the hotbar says why; some rooms have none to move.

5359.content: You were left in a shut ring of Saturn — wait for the next turn, it opens by itself.

5364.content: What the seals in dungeons and ruins wait for and how each lock works.

5369.content: Press Right-click on the sealed stone in a doorway: it tells what opens it — a key, rune plates, a beam, an ambush, a guard or the master.

5370.content: Rune plates: step on them in the order drawn on the wall. A wrong step puts all of them out — walk around the plates you have not lit yet.

5371.content: A beam: press Right-click on a mirror to turn it and lead the beam to the receiver.

5372.content: An ambush plate (a ring of runes on the floor) wakes when you are two steps inside: bars shut, waves come out where runes light up. Beat the last wave — the bars and the cache open.

5373.content: Fragile tiles crack and drop: step off at the first crack. Gas vents and beam traps show themselves before they fire.

5374.content: An ambush wakes only for a player in survival. If you leave or die, the bars open in 15 seconds; half a minute later it is ready again and continues from the same wave.

5375.content: A solved copy of a puzzle opens only its own doors. The altar of a master opens its treasury itself when the master falls.

5376.content: A plate stays dark — you lit it out of order: start again from the first sign.

5377.content: Stuck in an ambush with a foe out of reach — fifteen seconds without blows and it rises again beside you.

5380.content: Dungeons: what each one is about

5382.content: A dungeon of a world is several floors with a locked gate on each, a guard, and the master with a treasury at the bottom.

5387.content: Find the way: buy the chart from the elder of the people of this world (level 2; Hive, Breath, Eye and Neptune — 4; 10–14 emeralds and a compass).

5388.content: Bring food, a weapon, full air and charge. Refill columns on the way restore the oxygen and charge of a worn suit: press Right-click.

5389.content: On every floor find the gate and press Right-click on its keystone socket: it names the key and says in which room of this floor it lies and how it is hidden.

5390.content: Look for loose bricks near the walls: deep joints, a crack, dust blowing out. Press Right-click on them — the wall crumbles; behind it are caches and keys.

5391.content: Press Right-click with the key on the socket: the seals fall. The last floor leads to the arena and the altar of the master.

5392.content: Beat the master and press Right-click on treasury chests: everyone who fought takes a share of their own.

5393.content: While the master lives, the masonry cannot be dug: mining fatigue is on you in the whole dungeon. After the victory it lets go.

5394.content: A common chest is one for everybody, a treasury share is personal and once. Keys fit only their own floor of their own dungeon.

5395.content: “The masonry holds while the keeper lives: it will not yield to a pick” — do not dig: look for the key, a mechanism or a loose wall.

5396.content: The socket says nothing new — the hint is for this floor only: the room stands on the same floor, look behind every door.

5397.content: “The treasury knows only those who fought its keeper” — a share belongs to whoever took part in the fight.

5400.content: Dungeons: what each one is about

5401.content: Masters of worlds: how to summon

5403.content: The Atlas tab of the journal holds a card for every creature: where it lives, what it eats and how to keep it.

5408.content: Meet a creature: look at it from within 24 blocks (through a spyglass — up to 64).

5409.content: Study it: stay in sight within 16 blocks for half a minute and see it feeding, sleeping or hunting. A spyglass works from afar and twice as fast.

5410.content: Get a part of it: kill it or take it alive from those who give — shear, brush, pickaxe or bottle.

5411.content: Open the card: for 2 stardust it marks where to look for a kind you have not met.

5412.content: Study all that live in a world: you become its connoisseur.

5413.content: A study pays 1 stardust, a whole world 8. For a connoisseur the chance of trust is 1.5 times higher and the rest of a pair is half as long.

5414.content: What you did not finish watching is forgotten when you leave the game; what is studied stays.

5415.content: The bar does not grow — the creature is farther than 16 blocks, behind a wall or does nothing: wait till it feeds or goes somewhere.

5420.content: Awakened gates are linked: from any of them you step to any other, for a small toll.

5426.content: Find the ring: nine by nine frames with the gate heart below. In a world it stands in the open; on Earth a village astronomer sells the map.

5427.content: Press Right-click on the heart with an empty hand: the list shows conditions with marks and the price. Do all of them.

5428.content: Put the price in your inventory and press Right-click on the heart holding any of these things: everything is taken at once.

5429.content: Press Right-click on the awakened heart, choose gates in the list and step into the light: the toll is taken, you stand before the other ring.

5430.content: In the End and the Nether build a ring yourself: 27 frames and the heart below in the middle; the portal faces the one who puts the heart.

5431.content: Price of awakening: supply of the road (stardust, void shards or deep embers) 48–96, materials of the world, usually the heart of its master. The victory and a trial of the world (its event or a hunt) are asked too.

5432.content: Each passage costs 4 units of the supply of the road you leave from; while the parade of planets lasts on Earth, it is free.

5433.content: The End answers when the dragon is beaten and all rifts are torn, the Nether — when the wither is beaten and all vents are heard.

5434.content: “The gate does not answer yet” — the list says which condition is missing.

5435.content: “… frames missing” — the ring is incomplete: look at the empty places in the square, the corners stay empty.

5436.content: Placed a frame wrong — sneak and press Right-click with an empty hand: a frame or heart of an unfinished ring goes back to the inventory.

5438.content: Masters of worlds: how to summon

5441.content: A manual page, behind a spoiler.

5446.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

5447.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

5448.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

5451.content: Masters of worlds: how to summon

5453.content: Some beasts eat from your hand, and a fed pair has young — only under the sky of their own world.

5458.content: Learn the feed: it is the fruit of its world (the Atlas page of the beast names it). Hold it — the beast comes to you.

5459.content: Press Right-click on a grown beast, then on another of the same kind in half a minute: both are in love.

5460.content: Keep them together: a young one is born. Feed it — each treat takes a tenth off its growing time.

5461.content: Use shears, a bottle, a brush or a pickaxe on those who give something: wool, milk, wax, crystals — they grow back in a few minutes.

5462.content: Love lasts 30 s; the pair rests 5–7.5 minutes; the young grows up in 15–30 minutes.

5463.content: A beast gives young only in its own world, and not when there are more than 6–14 of its kind within 24 blocks (a list by species).

5464.content: An animal that is asleep at night wakes to the food.

5465.content: “…is in no mood for young here: this is not its sky” — carry it home or breed where it lives; eggs of the world do not help.

5466.content: “Too crowded” — take some away: the herd is at its limit.

5470.content: Masters of worlds: how to summon

5471.content: A manual page, behind a spoiler.

5476.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

5477.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

5478.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

5483.content: Once in a few days a meteorite falls in wild country, far from homes; it leaves a crater, metal and stardust.

5488.content: Go out for a walk in the wild: it falls only 80–120 blocks from a player and not nearer than 192 blocks to a bed of any player.

5489.content: Watch the sky: a fiery streak with a tail. The line on the screen tells the direction; the ground shakes first, the boom comes later.

5490.content: Walk to the pillar of smoke (at night — a glow; on the Moon — a white ray). It stands ten minutes or till the core is taken.

5491.content: Take the right pick: a stone one for ordinary crust, mesosiderite and comet cores; an iron one for iron, pallasite and meteorite cores.

5492.content: Break the crust around, then the core. The hot core burns the one who stands on it — crouch. Silk Touch takes the core whole.

5493.content: Tell the kind by the fire: orange — chondrite, gold — iron, yellow-green — pallasite, dull red — carbonaceous, crimson — mesosiderite, blue — comet, mint — tektite.

5494.content: Falls come every 2–5 days while somebody walks outside; most are small. The kind decides the crater: bowl, deep, shallow, a chain, a lake of ice, scattered glass.

5495.content: A giant is foretold three minutes ahead by a growing star; it falls 220–400 blocks away. The words about it go to those who built a refractor.

5496.content: The core of an ordinary (chondrite) meteorite awakens the gate of Earth; only it, not of other kinds.

5497.content: No meteorites for a long time — everybody sits at home or in a village: the schedule waits for someone in the wild.

5498.content: The smoke is gone — ten minutes passed or the core is taken: look for the crater where it was.

5499.content: “The meteor burned up in the sky” — the place became built up while it flew.

5504.content: Natives give tasks: bring, defeat, find, survive, deliver — and pay with things nobody else sells.

5510.content: Look for a gold “!” above a head (seen from 48 blocks). Press Right-click on that native.

5511.content: A talkative one shows the task above the answers: click that line or press Q. The others speak about it at once.

5512.content: Read the goals and the reward and choose “I'll do it.”. The first task you take appears in the corner of the screen by itself.

5513.content: Open the list any time: F7, the scroll button in the inventory or the Tasks tab of the journal. “Track” puts a task into the corner; the page tells the world and coordinates of the giver.

5514.content: A delivery: carry the parcel to the craft named in the goal, talk and choose “Hand it over.”.

5515.content: When the mark turns into a gold “?”, return and choose “Here, it's done.”: what was asked for is taken, the reward is given.

5517.content: Q in a talk — the task of this native

5518.content: “!” gold — new, blue — may be taken again (daily or every few days); “?” gray — taken, gold — ready or the parcel is with you.

5519.content: A native task counts creatures you have slain after taking it; places, events and masters count even if you did them before.

5520.content: You may hand a task to any native of that craft and people; a task marked “in person” — only to the one who gave it. Discounts add up to 30% at most.

5521.content: Gave up a task with a parcel — take it again, but the parcel is handed over only once: keep it.

5522.content: No “!” anywhere — some tasks open after others, after a landing on another world or a defeated master.

5526.content: Each of the worlds has its own people: they talk, trade, sell maps and keep tasks for you.

5531.content: Put a  on the rocket before the flight: right after landing it tells the distance and coordinates of the nearest settlement.

5532.content: Come up to a resident and press Right-click. Talkative ones greet you and offer topics, the others speak about their craft and show their goods.

5533.content: Choose an answer with the mouse or 1–9. Click the line to see all of it at once.

5534.content: Came only for goods? Hold Shift and press Right-click: trade opens without the talk.

5535.content: Trade with the elder until the level grows: the chart to the dungeon is sold at level 2 (Hive, Breath, Eye, Neptune — 4) for 10–14 emeralds and a compass.

5536.content: Ask craftspeople about their work: some point your compass at a place, some mend the item in your main hand, others tell where things live.

5537.content: Payment is emeralds and the currency of their world. Goods refill once a game day; levels grow with every deal, as with villagers.

5538.content: A gift or a secret from a talk is given once to each player; the natives remember the masters you have defeated and your answers.

5539.content: The chief has a crown above the mark, named masters a star: their tasks and goods are their own. A talk ends eight blocks away.

5540.content: “… backs away from you” — you hit this resident: the grudge lasts one minute.

5541.content: “… is hiding” — there is danger near or it was struck: wait till it calms down.

5542.content: “… is talking to someone else” — one player at a time.

5543.content: “Scanner: no settlements nearby” — land somewhere else: each people keeps to its own biomes.

5548.content: Feed a creature that can be tamed until it trusts you; in a harness of its world it carries you on land, in the air or water.

5555.content: Hold its treat (crystalline lens for the sclera grazer, float bladder for the storm ray, whale lumen for the whale, amberberries for the wader) and press Right-click again and again.

5556.content: Put on it the harness of its world: hold it and press Right-click.

5557.content: Press Right-click with an empty hand to sit in the saddle, Shift to get off. Press Right-click on an animal without a harness to make it sit or follow.

5558.content: Ride: turn with the mouse, W goes, Space jumps or lifts, Ctrl runs and tires it.

5559.content: To let it go, press Right-click sneaking with the treat in the other hand; take the harness off with shears.

5560.content: Shift + Right-click with an empty hand — sit or follow (also when saddled)

5561.content: Ctrl — faster while it has strength

5562.content: It trusts only the one who feeds; a blow or a stranger’s treat starts over. Nobody else can command it.

5563.content: Below 10% of strength it cannot run and a flyer glides down; rest, walk or feed to restore it.

5564.content: A ray flies where you look, a whale swims and does not leave the water — breathe with your own suit. A mount does not leave its world.

5565.content: “…is not yours” — another player tamed it: you may only feed it.

5566.content: It does not go up or run — the strength is out: wait a few seconds.

5579.content: Guide: Watch Rings and the Lens

5583.content: Structures of a world hide loot of that world and pages for the journal about the place.

5588.content: Look around from a height: most structures stand in the open, and settlements, gates and dungeon entrances have a light.

5589.content: Ask natives: cartographers point a compass at a structure, other crafts and elders sell charts.

5590.content: Come inside: the find is recorded when you walk into the structure itself.

5591.content: Open every chest and barrel and take the book out: a page about the place and loot of the world lie there.

5592.content: There are from seven to ten kinds of structures in a world; villages, gates and dungeons count too.

5593.content: Ruins with seals of puzzles (the halls of the Orphans) cannot be dug through until the last seal is gone.

5594.content: A door does not open — press Right-click on the sealed stone: it names what holds it.

5599.content: Signs on stones by the gates are words: you match pictures to them until the phrase makes sense.

5604.content: Find a gate ring and press Right-click on the dark stele on its platform. On Earth the map to the ring is sold by a village astronomer.

5605.content: Look at the fresco the stone shows: what is on it is what the words are about.

5606.content: Click a sign, then a picture you have met below. A wrong guess costs nothing; the secondary (right) mouse button clears it.

5607.content: When every sign has its right meaning, the phrase is read by itself; the same sign is lit in every inscription.

5608.content: Read more: each people remembers scraps — ask elders about signs; the court of the Lunarians has a stone with a translation.

5609.content: New pictures come from stones, the telescope and talks with peoples; the Lexicon tab of the journal keeps all signs.

5610.content: Your reading is yours: other players see their own. A sign stays known once the phrase has formed.

5611.content: A number stands on a line below, a name of a world — inside a ring, an action on a leg, a being — with a head: the shape tells the class.

5612.content: “The phrase does not come together” — some sign is guessed wrong: the fresco has everything the phrase is about.

5613.content: No picture for a sign — meet it first: look in the telescope, talk, read other stones.

5627.content: A giant that is not a stone: under the open sky it gathers stardust by night.

5632.content: Wait for a lilac star that grows in the sky: about three minutes later a heart falls 220–400 blocks from you. Go to it.

5633.content: Break the dark shell and the heart with an iron pick; a heart that fell gives 16–24 stardust, diamonds and presolar grains besides itself.

5634.content: Put it at home under the open sky. Sparks above it at night mean it gathers.

5635.content: Press Right-click on it to take what it has gathered, up to three stardust.

5636.content: It gathers only at night and only with open sky above the block; about two pinches a night. Presses pay nothing until it has something.

5637.content: The reward of a fallen one is given once: a heart you have put down gives only itself.

5638.content: It does not charge — something stands above it, or it is day.

5664.content: Thalassia is a second Earth by the star Hemera; the way there is a mouth by Jupiter’s Trojans; the first starship will do.

5669.content: Build the radio telescope and record the voice in Leo (it speaks for 4 minutes around its meridian, once a star day).

5670.content: Record it again on another star day or from another place (the Moon or an orbit): the shift gives the distance and the mouth appears on instruments.

5671.content: Fly by a starship: the mouth is 60° ahead of Jupiter, over the swarm of Trojans. Mark it on the system map.

5672.content: Jump close and steer right into the middle of the sphere with another sky inside: you come out near Hemera with the same course.

5673.content: Point at Thalassia, the turquoise moon of the blue giant Pontus, and enter its sky like any world.

5674.content: To go home fly into the Sol Mouth in the system of Hemera: it leads to the Trojans.

5675.content: The air is breathable, the water warm, the gravity 0.9 of Earth, the day 20 minutes: no suit or dome is needed, ordinary crops grow.

5676.content: At noon Pontus eclipses the sun for a few minutes; at night it lights the ground.

5677.content: “This window is already recorded” — the same window from the same place gives nothing new: wait for the next star day.

5678.content: The mouth is not on the map — only the one who has found it by radio or flown near sees it.

5683.content: Hemera oil and the liquids of Thalassia

5684.content: Hemera oil seeps out of ochre basalt and is the best natural fuel: a bucket burns longer than lava.

5689.content: Look in cliffs, rifts and on the column coast for ochre basalt with amber drips: a seep.

5690.content: Wait beside: it puts out a source every few minutes. Take it with a bucket by Right-click.

5691.content: Burn it: a bucket in a furnace lasts 32,000 ticks (lava 20,000, a coal block 16,000); fuel pipes carry it too, the Flame Separator eats it.

5692.content: Keep fire, lava and burning mobs away from a puddle: it goes up with a whoomp.

5693.content: A seep cannot be dug out — build beside it; several may stand in one cliff.

5694.content: Tidewater works as water but holds you up; boiling pitch burns, sticks three times harder than lava and turns to pitch crust in water; tide glow gives night vision for 30 s.

5695.content: Nothing flows — the place above the seep or beside its wall is closed or a source already stands there.

5699.content: Six plants of Thalassia’s sea live in tidewater; sea grapes are planted in any pond of it.

5704.content: Dive in the shallows or in the sea and break the plants of the bottom by hand.

5705.content: Carry tidewater in a bucket: the source multiplies, so a pond can stand anywhere, also on Earth.

5706.content: Plant sea grapes on the bottom of it — sand, silt, gravel, clay or mats.

5707.content: Use them: ribbonweed dries into a snack, three shoal grass make string, a tide fan — magenta dye, four barrel sponges — a wet sponge, a sea pen turns ink to glow ink.

5708.content: A plant of the sea stands only in a source of tidewater; game water beside it makes a hard edge. Grapes need no hydroponic bed and do not suit one.

5709.content: Night sea pens light up after sunset one by one; touch one in the dark and it flares up.

5710.content: The plant pops off — it stands not in tidewater or on the wrong ground.

5714.content: Thalassians live in hamlets on the meadows above the shallows and trade what keeps a second Earth useful.

5720.content: Find a hamlet on light meadows and windy hills above the shallows: wooden houses on stone footings with a pole of the eclipse in the middle.

5721.content: Talk to the elder and craftspeople: Right-click. Buy saplings, barley, stardust and air candles with emeralds and aquamarine.

5722.content: The weaver sells armor lining, module blanks and multitool modules (levels 4–5, one a day) and mends an item in your hand.

5723.content: Sow sea barley on farmland by the tidewater: four parasol saplings in a square grow a giant.

5724.content: At noon (the eclipse) the people rest; what they say of your garden changes when you have grown something yourself.

5725.content: Tidewater waters farmland like water, so beds may be anywhere by it.

5726.content: No hamlet near — they stand only on glowing meadows and downs, above the sea level.

5731.content: The cliff of Verona on Miranda is 270 blocks high; a snowdrift below takes a jump without harm.

5735.content: Climb the cliff from the east: the slope is long and gentle there.

5736.content: Walk out on the western gangway of the beacon at the edge and jump.

5737.content: Steer into the drift of ice dust at the foot, 40 blocks wide. It is 100 blocks of fall that count.

5738.content: With the gravity 0.06 you fall no faster than five blocks a second: the flight takes about a minute. Past the drift it hurts, but does not kill.

5739.content: It did not count — you fell less than 100 blocks or past the drift.

5741.content: Villagers of five new trades; their work blocks are machines of this mod.

5746.content: Place a work block near a villager with no profession (not a nitwit): a refractor telescope, drafting table, fuel plant, charging station or hydroponic bed.

5747.content: Wait until the villager walks up to it: its clothes change.

5748.content: Press Right-click on the villager and trade: every trade gives experience and opens higher levels.

5749.content: Find houses of these crafts in generated villages of the Earth as well.

5750.content: Astronomer (refractor): buys amethyst, glass, copper; sells optical glass 2 for 1 emerald, lens blank 3, polished lens 6, 2 stardust 6, mirrors.

5751.content: Rocket engineer (drafting table): hull plates 4 for 2, heat tiles 4 for 2, wiring 6 for 3, nozzle 6, turbopump 10, combustion chamber 12, avionics 18.

5752.content: Fuel technician (fuel plant): canister 2 for 3, fuel canister for 2 and an empty one, helium-3 for 3, 8 regolith and an empty one at level 4. Power engineer (charging station): battery 3, charged for 1 and a flat one, solar cell 6, charging station 28.

5753.content: Hydroponist (bed): buys bone meal, pumpkins, melons; sells 6 bread for 1, 3 golden carrots for 3, a golden apple 14, a hydroponic bed 10.

5754.content: The villager did not change — it is a nitwit, already has a trade, or cannot reach the block.

5755.content: The trade is out — it restocks at the work block twice a day.

5783.content: Every few days something big happens in a world; who stays there to the end has survived it.

5788.content: Be in a world and wait for the banner with the name of the event. Events happen only while a player is there.

5789.content: Read the line below the name and watch the ground: rings of fire, runes, cracks or ringing mark the dangerous place ahead of time.

5790.content: Hide or go close: step out of the marked spot, and look for the reward by the danger itself.

5791.content: Stay alive in this world till the end of the event, anywhere in it: the stage and gates count it for everyone there.

5792.content: Most events come every 4–10 days and last 4–8 minutes; eclipses take about two minutes, the parade of planets 3 days, the supernova 4.

5793.content: A bed does not work while an event shorter than a day is on; an eclipse missed by sleep comes another night.

5794.content: The event of a world gate never comes — wait longer or come again: each world has three events, one of them is on the list of the gates.

5795.content: It did not count — you were in another world (or dead) when it ended.

5799.content: Each world has two or three ores of its own in its own rock; they pay for almost everything the worlds give.

5804.content: Look for a speckled spot of another color in the bare rock of the world: cliffs, caves and crater walls show veins best.

5805.content: Take the right pick: an ordinary stone one for cinnabar, sulfur, ammonia, amber…; iron for most; diamond for iridium, adamant, black diamond and osmiridium.

5806.content: Smelt raw ore in a furnace, or crush it first in the crusher: two dusts instead of one ingot.

5807.content: No vein in sight? Use the multitool scanner or the ore scanner: they show veins through the rock.

5808.content: In the clouds of gas giants the ore hangs as solid blocks in the cloud: look for a cross of light of its color, seen up to 28 blocks away.

5809.content: Other mods know these ores by the common “c:” tags; five families of Thalassia are parted by the Flame Separator.

5810.content: Nothing drops — the pick is too weak for this ore; adamant, iridium and black diamond need a diamond one.

5813.content: Weather comes and goes by itself and slightly changes the world: what you breathe, see, and how you move.

5818.content: Stay in a world and look at the sky: the stage is done when one weather reaches full strength while you are there.

5819.content: Hail and micrometeorites: wear a helmet or stand under a roof.

5820.content: Wind: crouch or go under a roof — it carries you away from heights.

5821.content: Use the good ones: ores settle out of hail, an exhalation gives air, light pillars show where to dig, a fog hides you.

5822.content: It lasts minutes and comes without a banner; some kinds come only at dawn, dusk or night.

5823.content: Micrometeorites and hail hurt only those under open sky with no helmet; the helmet itself wears out instead.

5824.content: A compass spins — on Earth the aurora pulls it; wait for dawn.

5883.content: The mod’s three roads — the sky, the dark and the fire — briefly and without spoilers.

5888.content:
The mod has three roads. Each starts with its own instrument, leads through its own worlds and needs its own transport.
You can take any of them in any order, but the journal leads along the sky road first.

5889.content:
It starts with a telescope on Earth. Telescopes grow — refractor, reflector, astrograph, graviscope — and each sees
further: first the constellations and the Moon, then the planets. A world you have found can be visited by rocket: the
lunar, interplanetary, heavy and deep-space rockets fly further and further. Beyond that the road leads to your own
ships and open space.

5890.content:
The road’s worlds are the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, the giant planets and their small worlds. In detail — in the
world reference. From Jupiter’s trojans a throat leads to another star and a second Earth —
Thalassia.

5891.content:
It starts in the End. The riftscope looks not at the stars but into the void: rifts hide in it, and you have to find
them and tear them open along the seam. Beyond the rifts lie four worlds, reached by the **shuttle**. See
“Riftscope”. How it ends — behind a spoiler.

5892.content:
It starts in the Nether. The magmascope looks down into a bowl of lava: vents are found by ear and opened with strikes
in time with their pulse. At the bottom of the vents lie worlds of fire, reached by the **bell**. See
“Magmascope”. How it ends — behind a spoiler.

5893.content: Every world has a **master** — a boss at the heart of that world’s dungeon. While it lives, the world’s gate sleeps.

5894.content:
**Gates** — nine-by-nine rings on all the worlds at once. Awakened gates link the worlds, bypassing transport.
See “Gates”.

5895.content:
**Peoples** live on many worlds: you trade with them, talk to them and take their tasks. See
“Peoples and tasks”.

5898.content: The mod on a dedicated server: installation, playing together and server load.

5901.content: The mod is made for playing with friends: everything works on a dedicated server with several players.

5902.content:
**Installed on the server and on every player** — the same versions of the mod and its dependencies, the same
Minecraft version (26.3, 1.21.1 or 1.20.1) and the same loader, Fabric, NeoForge or Forge (see “Installation”).
Servers on 1.20.1 run on Java 17, servers on 1.21.1 on Java 21, servers on 26.3 on Java 25.

5903.content:
**Everyone has their own path**: the journal, found worlds, the spacesuit, tasks and the trust of the peoples are
per player. Worlds, buildings and gates are shared.

5904.content: **Together** you can fly in one rocket, crew a ship, transfer to a friend’s ship and tow a downed ship.

5905.content:
**Knowledge by copy**: to catch up with a friend who has gone ahead, use a Journal Copy: it carries
stages, finds, the Atlas of Life and other knowledge, while deeds (landings, victories, rewards) stay each player's own.

5906.content:
**Your station for a team**: the owner lets friends onto their own station with the Station team window or the `station trust`
command, see Your own station: team and name.

5907.content:
**Sleep and events**: while one of a world's events is on (the blood moon and the rest), nobody can sleep there: the bed names
the event but still sets the spawn point, and an event wakes those asleep. Other worlds sleep as usual. Sleeping through the
night of a lunar eclipse before it begins moves the eclipse to the next night at the same hour — it never starts in daylight;
a night aurora also fades once the night is slept away.

5908.content:
**Your seat waits for you**: if you leave the game aboard a ship you were not flying alone, the seat stays yours — when
you come back you are aboard again, in your own seat, wherever the ship has got to by then. A crew also survives a server
restart: the ship is in place and everyone is seated. Alone aboard, the ship still leaves the world with you and returns
with you, as before. The same holds in a rocket, the End shuttle and the Nether bell with a passenger seat: leave during
lift-off and you come back into your seat wherever the craft is flying; if it has landed without you, you step out
beside it, next to the others. If the craft is gone (the ship was destroyed while you were away), you are brought to
safety — to the ground nearby or to your respawn point — and if your seat has been taken, the ship lets you aboard, on
the deck. A line on the screen tells you so.

5909.content:
**Light on the server**: the mod does not walk every block and entity every tick, does heavy work less often and on
events, and sends packets only on change. This is checked by measuring on a server with players.

5910.content:
**Fast flight does not stall the server**: chunks along a ship’s course are prepared in advance, and where they are
still being generated the server does not wait for them mid-tick. Light under growing islands and boss beams are sent
sparingly — in one packet and as keyframes.

5911.content:
The client only draws and sends intentions — the server decides: whether a world is found, a stage is counted, a
rocket has arrived.

5912.content:
**Checked by two players.** Before release the whole mod is walked through by two players on a real dedicated server,
on Fabric and on NeoForge: 63 scenes, from joining and machine windows to ships, small worlds and their events, the far roads and the
finale, with players leaving mid-flight, dropped connections and a server restart. After a drop and after the restart
everything a player has is compared: world and place, progress, spacesuit, tasks, inventory, the ship under them.

5913.content:
**A stop in the middle of the Free Haven fight.** The raiders' lair on Deimos keeps in the world data how many of its
ships and turrets are still standing and how much damage each player has dealt to them. After a server restart the
surviving defenders come out again, and the shares of those who fought before the stop are intact. The journal key for
sacking the haven also waits for a player who fought its defenders but was offline when it fell: they get it a few
seconds after joining. The share items themselves lie by the haven for twelve minutes
(a downed raider's wreck — three), and a server restart does not wipe them: the spoils are kept in the world data, each
share waits for its own player and nobody else can take it — fly by in a ship and it goes into the hold.

5914.content:
**Nether and End changes.** The Nether and the End change in stages, shared by the whole server, as players open rifts, vents
and the roads beyond them (Nether and End changes). A server owner can switch the changes off with
the game rule Nether and End changes (`/gamerule`, under the mod id, `nether_end_changes`) or with
`"nether_end_changes": false` in `config/<mod id>-server.json`: stages still build up, but nothing is shown.

5915.content:
**Cargo nodes.** A Quantum Cargo Node may load the chunks of its far end for a minute to take things from there, at the cost of its charge and for four far ends at most.
Switch that off with the game rule Wake far ends of cargo nodes (`cargo_wake` under the mod id): then nodes only send and show the last list.

5916.content:
**The mod has one command**, named the same as the mod id; it needs operator rights. To run it for a player, use
`execute as <player> run …`.

5917.content:
| Command                | What it does                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `progress grant <key>` | counts one progress key: to restore something lost. `progress complete` and `progress reset` set the whole journal path at once |

5918.content:
| Command                                   | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `structure restore <id> [radius] [force]` | puts a mod structure into the world of whoever gave the command, where it belongs — for old worlds whose chunks were generated without it (up to 0.15.2 the Ring at the Edge and other one-per-world structures were missing in some worlds, and `/locate` hung on them). It searches from the caller outwards (3072 blocks by default), records the structure so `/locate` finds it, and does not clear what already stands there; `force` places it again |

5919.content:
| Command                | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rocket land [player]` | lands a craft (rocket, shuttle, bell) stuck in flight: the one the player sits in (without a player — the caller), or, if they are not aboard one, the nearest craft taking off, on its way or waiting over a world. A craft that has not left yet is moved to the world it is flying to, onto its usual landing site; the flight ends for those aboard, and the craft lands and turns back into blocks. It should not get stuck anyway: over the new world a craft waits for its passengers no longer than 15 seconds, and the player's space scene ends by itself when they are not aboard |

5920.content:
| Command               | What it does                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `raid [count] [warn]` | sends raiders at the ship of whoever gave the command — an ambush at once or a raid after a warning. Needs a pilot in survival mode in open space, away from stations |

5921.content:
| Command                      | What it does                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `act flight [x y z] <world>` | “fly” in a rocket, shuttle or bell (without a place — the nearest cabin), with all the game’s checks |

5922.content:
| Command                                          | What it does                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `act jump <body>`, `act far auto\|back <target>` | a ship jump; a stitch, a dive and the return along the mark |

5923.content:
| Command    | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `act lair` | where the raiders' lair is and its state: how many defenders are still standing and how many are out, how many players hold a share, who is owed the key; how many spoils shares are waiting in space and how many items they hold |

5924.content:
| Command                          | What it does                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stage end\|nether [get\|set N]` | the stage of the End or Nether changes in this world: read it or set it |

5925.content:

5926.content:

| `meteor [<kind> [size [distance [warning seconds]]]]` | drops a meteorite of that kind near whoever gave the command, here and now; `meteor natural` — by the rules of the schedule |
